definition_zh: 宽容的；容忍的；能耐的（可容忍某条件）
definition_en: willing to accept ways of thinking or behaving that differ from your own
core_image: 一个人张开双臂，让不同的声音从他身边安然穿过
scene: 老师对班上的不同观点始终保持宽容。The teacher stayed tolerant of every different view in her class.
sceneCN: 这里 tolerant 是「宽容的」（第 1 个义项：愿意接受与自己不同的想法和行为）；句意：老师对班上的不同观点始终保持宽容。

pos.zh: 能耐的；能容许……的（医学、植物学）

derivatives.zh: 由 tolerate 加 -ance 构成的名词，义为「宽容；耐受度」
由拉丁语 tolerare 加英语词尾构成的动词，义为「容忍；忍受」
由 tolerate 加 -ion 构成，义为「容许；宗教宽容」
由否定前缀 in- 加 tolerant 构成，义为「不宽容的」
由拉丁语 tolerare 加 -able 构成，义为「可忍受的」

senses.title: Willing to accept different views
senses.definition: willing to accept beliefs, customs, or ways of behaving that differ from your own
senses.definitionCN: 愿意接受与自己不同的信仰、习俗或行为方式
senses.example: A tolerant teacher listens before correcting.
senses.exampleCN: 宽容的老师会先听完再纠正。
senses.why: Latin tolerare means to bear or put up with, and the suffix -ant marks a person who bears, so tolerant describes someone willing to carry differences without anger.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tolerare 意为「承受、忍受」，后缀 -ant 表示进行者，所以 tolerant 形容一个人愿意不带怒气地承载差异。

senses.title: Allowing a practice without opposing it
senses.titleCN: 容许的；不反对某做法的
senses.definition: permitting an activity or group to exist without trying to stop it
senses.definitionCN: 允许某项活动或群体存在而不去制止
senses.example: The city is tolerant of street music.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市容许街头音乐。
senses.why: Once bearing becomes a social stance, the word names the attitude of a group that leaves something in place instead of driving it out.
senses.whyCN: 当「承受」变成一种社会立场，这个词便指一个群体「让某种事物留在原处而不是驱赶它」的态度。

senses.title: Able to endure a hard condition
senses.titleCN: 能耐的；耐得住某种条件的
senses.definition: able to withstand an unpleasant condition such as heat, drought, or a drug without harm
senses.definitionCN: 能承受炎热、干旱或某种药物等不利条件而不受损害
senses.example: This crop is tolerant of salt and drought.
senses.exampleCN: 这种作物耐盐又耐旱。
senses.why: The root meaning of bearing survives in science: a plant or patient that bears heat or a drug is literally able to carry it.
senses.whyCN: 「承受」的本义在科学中保留下来：能耐受高温或药物的植物或病人，字面上就是「能承载得住」。

senses.title: Showing little reaction to an unwanted effect
senses.titleCN: 有耐受性的；反应迟钝的
senses.definition: showing a weaker reaction than usual to something that once affected you strongly, such as a medicine or a sound
senses.definitionCN: 对曾经强烈影响自己的东西（如药物或声音）反应比平常弱
senses.example: Patients become tolerant to the drug after weeks of use.
senses.exampleCN: 病人用药数周后会对这种药产生耐受性。
senses.why: Enduring something again and again dulls the response, so the same bearing idea also names reduced sensitivity in medicine.
senses.whyCN: 反复承受同一种刺激会让反应变钝，于是同一个「承受」概念也用来指医学上敏感度降低。

intro.en: Tolerant comes from Latin tolerare, to bear or endure, through the present participle tolerans.
intro.cn: tolerant 来自拉丁语 tolerare（承受、忍受），经由现在分词 tolerans 进入英语。

items.en: Tolerare means to bear, endure, or put up with; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: tolerare 意为承受、忍受；其更深词源不确定。

items.en: Tolerans is the present participle, one who is bearing.
items.cn: tolerans 是现在分词，意为「正在承受的人」。

items.en: Tolerant enters English and later settles into the meaning of putting up with things patiently.
items.cn: tolerant 进入英语，后来固定为耐心容忍的意思。

items.en: Political and religious writers use tolerant for accepting other beliefs.
items.cn: 政治与宗教作者用 tolerant 表示接受其他信仰。

items.en: Medical and botanical uses add the ability to bear a drug or a hard condition.
items.cn: 医学与植物学用法增加了「能耐受药物或恶劣条件」之义。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the social sense and the biological one, as in salt tolerant crops.
items.cn: 现代英语兼有社会义与生物义，如耐盐作物。

note.en: Tolerant is the adjective of the tolerate family and sits near the wider words for accepting difference.
note.cn: tolerant 是 tolerate 词族的形容词，与更宽泛的「接受差异」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to allow or endure something you dislike
entries.definitionCN: 容忍；忍受（不喜欢的）某事

entries.definition: the quality of being tolerant
entries.definitionCN: 宽容；耐受度

entries.definition: unwilling to accept different views
entries.definitionCN: 不宽容的；不容异见的

entries.definition: not strict in punishing people
entries.definitionCN: 宽大的；不严格的，多指处罚上从轻

entries.definition: willing to accept opinions unlike your own
entries.definitionCN: 心胸开阔的；能接受不同意见的

entries.definition: able to wait or endure difficulties calmly
entries.definitionCN: 有耐心的；能平静忍受困难的

normalIntro.en: Tolerant keeps the Latin picture of bearing a load, and its family shows every change of role.
normalIntro.cn: tolerant 保留拉丁语「承载负荷」的画面，其词族展示了各种词性变化。

normal.en: Tolerant is the adjective, and the adverb is tolerantly, as in she answered tolerantly.
normal.cn: tolerant 是形容词，副词是 tolerantly，如她宽容地回答。

normal.en: Tolerance is the noun, so a tolerant person shows tolerance.
normal.cn: tolerance 是名词：宽容的人表现出宽容。

normal.en: Tolerant of and tolerant towards are the usual patterns before the thing accepted.
normal.cn: tolerant of 与 tolerant towards 是表示所容忍对象的常用搭配。

normal.en: The prefix in- makes intolerant, the opposite of tolerant.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 构成 intolerant，是 tolerant 的反义。

normal.en: In science tolerant of salt and heat describes plant ability, not attitude.
normal.cn: 科学语境里 tolerant of salt and heat 描述植物的耐性，而不是态度。

abstract.en: See someone hold a heavy bag for another without complaint, jaw set, still willing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人替别人拎着沉重的包，一声抱怨也没有，咬着牙但仍愿意。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing calmly between two groups who disagree.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人平静地站在两个意见相左的群体之间。

abstract.en: Think of a plant on cracked salty soil that keeps its leaves green.
abstract.cn: 想象一株长在开裂盐土上的植物，叶子仍然是绿的。

examples.en: The school is tolerant of different faiths and customs.
examples.cn: 这所学校对不同信仰和习俗都很宽容。

examples.en: Researchers bred a variety tolerant of both salt and drought.
examples.cn: 研究人员培育出一个既耐盐又耐旱的品种。

examples.en: She spoke tolerantly about the neighbours who played music late.
examples.cn: 她谈起床很晚还放音乐的邻居时语气宽容。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「透了然的」——把别人的差异看透了、想开了，就变得宽容；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tolerare（承受、忍受，词源不确定）→ tolerans（正在承受的）→ 英语 tolerant。后缀 -ant 表示进行者，核心义「愿意承载」。

sensesIntro.en: Tolerant starts from bearing a difference, moves to the social stance of allowing it, and then to the physical ability to endure heat, salt, or a drug.
sensesIntro.cn: tolerant 从「承受差异」出发，转为社会层面「容许」的态度，再转为身体上耐热、耐盐、耐受药物的能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone holding up a heavy load without complaint.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人不抱怨地扛着一副重担。

branches.en: Accepting other views is the personal sense.
branches.cn: 接受他人观点是个人层面的义项。

branches.en: Allowing a practice to remain is the social sense.
branches.cn: 容许某种做法继续存在是社会层面的义项。

branches.en: Enduring heat or salt is the biological sense.
branches.cn: 耐受高温或盐分是生物层面的义项。

branches.en: A tolerant person and a tolerant city both refuse to drive the other side away.
branches.cn: 宽容的人与宽容的城市都不把对方赶走。

branches.en: Science extends bearing a condition into reduced sensitivity after repeated exposure.
branches.cn: 科学把「承受条件」延伸到反复接触后的敏感度降低。

intro.en: Tolerant is built from the Latin verb tolerare plus the suffix -ant, and its family covers verb, noun, and adjective.
intro.cn: tolerant 由拉丁语动词 tolerare 加后缀 -ant 构成，其词族覆盖动词、名词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tolerare means to bear or endure, and tolerans is its present participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tolerare 意为承受、忍受，tolerans 是它的现在分词。

items.example: Tolerare supplies the bearing image.
items.exampleCN: tolerare 提供「承载」的意象。

items.meaning: one that does or is doing
items.meaningCN: 表示进行者或具有某种性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ant forms tolerant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 构成 tolerant。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ance forms tolerance.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ance 构成 tolerance。

items.example: The ending -ate helps form tolerate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 参与构成 tolerate。

items.example: The suffix -able forms tolerable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 tolerable。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms toleration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 toleration。

items.example: The prefix in- forms intolerant.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 intolerant。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms tolerantly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 tolerantly。

items.example: Tolerate is the verb behind tolerant.
items.exampleCN: tolerate 是 tolerant 背后的动词。

definition_zh: 厚书；大本书；卷册
definition_en: a large heavy book, especially one that is old or part of a scholarly set
core_image: 一本沉重的大书压在桌角，书脊厚得能当砖头
scene: 书架上那本厚重的巨册落满了灰。Nobody had opened the dusty tome on the top shelf for years.
sceneCN: 这里 tome 是「厚书、巨册」（第 1 个义项：厚重的大部头书）；句意：顶层书架上那本落满灰尘的巨册多年没人翻过。

collocations.phrase: the first tome of the series

derivatives.zh: 希腊语 tomos 表「切片」的后缀，用于 anatomy 解剖学等，与书义的 tome 同源于「切开」
由希腊语否定前缀 a- 加 tomos（切开）构成，原义「不可再切分者」，与 tome 共享「切」的词根
由希腊语 epi-（在上）加 temnein（切）构成，义为「摘要；典型」，词根与 tome 相关
由 tome 加 -ful 构成的非正式形容语，指厚得像一本大部头

senses.title: A large heavy book
senses.definition: a very large and heavy book, often old and read with effort
senses.definitionCN: 一本很大很重的书，往往年迈而读来费力
senses.example: He carried a heavy tome under one arm.
senses.exampleCN: 他腋下夹着一本厚重的大书。
senses.why: Greek tomos means a piece cut off, and a section of a long work was once a cut piece of text; English gave that piece the size of a big volume.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 tomos 意为「切下的一块」，长篇作品的一段曾被视为切下的一块文本；英语再给它添上「大卷册」的分量。

senses.title: One volume of a set
senses.definition: one of several volumes into which a long work or set is divided
senses.definitionCN: 一部长篇作品或一套书被分成的若干卷册之一
senses.example: Only the second tome of the dictionary survived.
senses.exampleCN: 那部词典只剩下了第二卷。
senses.why: The piece cut from a book is literally a volume, so tome also names a numbered part of a larger work.
senses.whyCN: 从整部书里切下来的一块，字面上就是一册，所以 tome 也指大部作品里编号的一部分。

senses.title: A big book that shows off weight
senses.definition: a book described as big and heavy, often in a slightly mocking or humorous tone
senses.definitionCN: 被形容为又大又重的书，常带一点揶揄或幽默的语气
senses.example: She packed a seven-hundred-page tome for a weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 她为周末带了一本七百页的大部头。
senses.why: Because the word stresses bulk rather than content, critics and reviewers use it to tease authors who write very long books.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词强调体积而非内容，评论者就用它打趣写超长作品的作者。

senses.title: The manuscript volume of old studies
senses.definition: a bound volume of an old hand-written or early printed scholarly work, such as medieval or classical texts
senses.definitionCN: 装订成册的古手稿或早期印刷学术作品，如中世纪或古典文本
senses.example: Scholars spent a decade restoring the ancient tomes.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们花了十年修复那些古籍卷册。
senses.why: The book sense of tome entered English through French for a part of a classical text, so it keeps a scholarly, historical colour.
senses.whyCN: tome 的书义经法语进入英语，原指古典文本的一个部分，因此至今带着学术与历史的色彩。

intro.en: Tome comes from Greek tomos, a piece cut off and hence a roll or volume, through Latin tomus and Old French tome.
intro.cn: tome 源自希腊语 tomos（切下的一块，引申为书卷、卷册），经拉丁语 tomus 与古法语 tome 进入英语。

items.en: Temnein means to cut, and tomos means a piece cut off, used for a section of a text.
items.cn: temnein 意为切割，tomos 意为切下的一块，用来指文本的一个部分。

items.en: Tomus keeps the sense of a section or roll of writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tomus 保留「一段文字、一卷」的含义。

items.en: Tome carries the word into French as one part of a classical work.
items.cn: 古法语 tome 一词把该词引入，指古典作品的一个部分。

items.en: Tome is first used in English for a volume of a work.
items.cn: tome 首次在英语中用于著作的卷册。

items.en: The sense widens to any very large heavy book.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何厚重的大书。

items.en: Modern English often uses tome humorously for books that stress weight over content.
items.cn: 现代英语常用 tome 略带戏谑地指重体积胜过内容的书。

note.en: Tome is a book word for weight and learning, close to its Greek cutting root and to the plain volume.
note.cn: tome 是表示厚重与学问的书本类词，与它的希腊语「切」词根以及普通的 volume 相邻。

entries.definition: a particle once thought to be unable to be cut
entries.definitionCN: 曾被认为不可再切的粒子，与 tome 共享「切」的词根

entries.definition: the study of the body by cutting it apart
entries.definitionCN: 解剖学，含与 tome 同源的「切」

entries.definition: a tool that is pulled through hair
entries.definitionCN: 梳子；只在拼写上相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a book, often one of a numbered set
entries.definitionCN: 书；卷册，常指成套书中的一册

entries.definition: a set of printed pages bound together
entries.definitionCN: 书，最普通的说法

entries.definition: a text written by hand rather than printed
entries.definitionCN: 手稿；手抄本

normalIntro.en: Tome ties weight to the Greek idea of a cut piece, so a volume is literally a section cut from a bigger text.
normalIntro.cn: tome 把重量与希腊语「切下的一块」联系起来：一卷书字面上就是从更大的文本里切下的一段。

normal.en: The plural is simply tomes, so several heavy books are tomes.
normal.cn: 复数只是加 s，几本厚书就是 tomes。

normal.en: Greek temnein means to cut, the root shared with anatomy and atom.
normal.cn: 希腊语 temnein 意为切割，anatomy、atom 与 tome 共享这个词根。

normal.en: Tome and volume can both mean a book, but tome adds bulk and age.
normal.cn: tome 与 volume 都能指书，但 tome 多了厚重与古旧的味道。

normal.en: Book reviews use a tongue in cheek tone with a seven hundred page tome.
normal.cn: 书评里用 seven hundred page tome 这类说法，常常带着戏谑的语气。

normal.en: Tome describes objects and learning, so it suits a library and not a message of feeling.
normal.cn: tome 描述实物与学术，适合图书馆的场景，而不适合表达情感的话语。

abstract.en: Picture a brick-thick book on a library shelf, corners worn by decades of use.
abstract.cn: 想象图书馆架上一本砖头厚的书，书角被几十年的翻阅磨白了。

abstract.en: Feel the ache in your wrists after carrying one heavy book up the stairs.
abstract.cn: 体会把一本厚书抱上楼梯后手腕的酸胀。

abstract.en: Think of a book cut into three thick slabs, each one numbered as a tome.
abstract.cn: 想象一部书被切成三块厚砖，每一块都编号成一卷。

examples.en: The old tome was bound in cracked brown leather.
examples.cn: 这本古籍用开裂的棕色皮革装订。

examples.en: Move the tomes down two shelves before you dust them.
examples.cn: 掸灰之前先把那些厚卷挪到下面两层书架上。

examples.en: His latest tome runs to more than nine hundred pages.
examples.cn: 他最新的大部头足有九百多页。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偷摸」——厚重的古籍只能待在架子上，想拿下来都得偷偷摸摸地搬；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 temnein（切割）→ tomos（切下的一块，引申为卷册）→ 拉丁语 tomus → 古法语 tome → 英语 tome。核心义「切分下的一卷」。

sensesIntro.en: Tome begins as a cut section of a text, becomes one volume of a set, then any heavy book and a slightly mocking word for big books.
sensesIntro.cn: tome 起初指切下的一段文本，后来指成套书中的一册，再泛指任何厚重的书，最终成为略带戏谑的大部头之称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick heavy book lying on the corner of a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本厚重的大书压在桌角。

branches.en: A heavy book is the ruling everyday sense.
branches.cn: 厚书是占主导的日常义项。

branches.en: One numbered volume of a set is the sectional sense.
branches.cn: 成套书里编号的一册是分部义项。

branches.en: The mocking tone for an oversized book colours the word.
branches.cn: 对大部头的戏谑语气给这个词上了色。

branches.en: A volume of an ancient work carries the scholarly and historical colour.
branches.cn: 古籍作品的卷册承载了学术与历史的色彩。

branches.en: Both bulk senses come from the same cutting root, since a section is a piece of a text.
branches.cn: 两种体积义都出自同一个「切」的词根，因为一段就是文本的一块。

intro.en: Tome is a noun of the cutting root seen in anatomy and atom, and its English family is thin.
intro.cn: tome 是带有「切」词根的名词，同根词见于 anatomy、atom，其英语词族很单薄。

latinIntro.en: Latin tomus supplies the section meaning, from Greek tomos cut from temnein to cut.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tomus 提供「卷段」之义，其源头为希腊语 tomos，来自表示切割的 temnein。

items.example: Temnein is the ultimate root of tome.
items.exampleCN: temnein 是 tome 的最终词根。

items.meaning: a piece cut off, a section
items.example: Tomos becomes a section of a text.
items.exampleCN: tomos 成为文本的一段。

items.meaning: a roll, a section of writing
items.example: Tomus carries the word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: tomus 把该词带入拉丁语。

items.example: Tome is the modern English form.
items.exampleCN: tome 是现代英语形式。

items.example: The suffix -s forms tomes.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 tomes。

items.example: The prefix a- appears in atom.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 a- 见于 atom。

items.example: The suffix -tomy appears in anatomy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tomy 见于 anatomy。

items.example: The prefix epi- appears in epitome.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 epi- 见于 epitome。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms tomeful.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ful 构成 tomeful。

latinEntries.meaning: a section or roll of writing

definition_zh: 补药；补品；滋补的；使精神振作的；主音的；主音；汤力水
definition_en: something that gives strength or energy, or a medicine that makes you feel stronger
core_image: 一杯苦味药水，喝完人从瘫软里重新绷紧起来
scene: 长途跋涉后，一杯浓茶让人重新有了力气。After the long walk, a cup of strong tea was a real tonic.
sceneCN: 这里 tonic 是「滋补品、提神之物」（第 1 个义项：让人恢复力气或精神的东西）；句意：长途步行后，一杯浓茶简直是补药。

pos.zh: 滋补的；使精神振作的；主音的

derivatives.zh: 无张力的；松弛的（a- 否定 + tonic）
高渗的（hyper- 过度 + tonic，医学用语）
张力；紧张度（tonic + -ity 名词后缀）

senses.title: A medicine or drink that restores strength
senses.definition: a medicine or drink that is thought to make you feel stronger or healthier
senses.definitionCN: 据信能使人变强壮或更健康的药物或饮料
senses.example: People once drank bitters as a daily tonic.
senses.exampleCN: 过去人们把苦味酒当作每日补药来喝。
senses.why: Greek tonikos means fit for stretching, coming from tonos, a stretching or tension, so a tonic first stretches slackened strength back into place.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 tonikos 意为「适合拉紧的」，来自 tonos（拉紧、张力），所以补药最初就是把松垮的力气重新拉紧的东西。

senses.title: Something that lifts the spirits
senses.definition: an activity or experience that makes you feel happy and energetic again
senses.definitionCN: 使人重新愉快、有干劲的活动或经历
senses.example: Her visit was a tonic for the lonely old man.
senses.exampleCN: 她的来访对这位孤独的老人是一剂提神的良药。
senses.why: If a medicine can tighten the body, the same word can tighten the mood, so any cheering event becomes metaphorical medicine.
senses.whyCN: 药物既能把身体重新绷紧，同一个词也能把心情重新绷紧，于是任何让人振奋的事都成了比喻意义上的药。

senses.title: The first and main note of a key
senses.definition: the first note of a musical scale, on which the key rests
senses.definitionCN: 一个音阶的第一个音，调性落点所在的音
senses.example: The melody keeps returning to the tonic.
senses.exampleCN: 这段旋律不断回到主音上。
senses.why: Music repeats the body image: the tonic is the note that pulls tension back to its resting point.
senses.whyCN: 音乐沿用了身体的意象：主音就是那个把张力拉回安放点的音。

senses.title: Bitter fizzy water used as a mixer
senses.definition: a carbonated drink flavoured with quinine, often mixed with gin
senses.definitionCN: 用奎宁调味的碳酸饮料，常与金酒混合
senses.example: A gin and tonic uses far more tonic than gin.
senses.exampleCN: 一杯金汤力里，汤力水远比金酒多。
senses.why: Quinine water was sold as a malaria tonic, and the English-speaking world kept the medicinal word for the drink.
senses.whyCN: 含奎宁的水当年是以防治疟疾的补药名义出售的，英语世界就把这个带药味的词留给了这种饮料。

senses.title: Giving strength or an energising quality
senses.definition: having the quality of making a person feel strong or refreshed
senses.definitionCN: 具有使人变强壮或神清气爽之性质的
senses.example: Mountain air has a tonic effect on the lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 山间空气对肺有滋补功效。
senses.why: The noun sense became an adjective, so anything with the power of a tonic is tonic itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词的滋补义转成形容词，于是凡是带着补药般功效的东西都可以用 tonic 形容。

intro.en: Tonic goes back to Greek tonos, a stretching or tension, through the medical adjective tonikos and Latin tonicus.
intro.cn: tonic 可上溯希腊语 tonos（拉紧、张力），经医学形容词 tonikos 与拉丁语 tonicus 进入英语。

items.en: Tonos means a stretching, tension, or tone.
items.cn: tonos 意为拉紧、张力、音调。

items.en: Tonikos is the adjective for what relates to tension.
items.cn: tonikos 是与张力有关的形容词。

items.en: Medical Latin tonicus means relating to tension or tone.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语 tonicus 意为与张力或音调有关的。

items.en: English tonic first names medicines that tone up the body.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 tonic 先指使身体恢复张力的药物。

items.en: Tonic spreads to music, where the tonic is the key note.
items.cn: 其后 tonic 扩展到音乐，指调式的主音。

items.en: Tonic water takes the medical label into ordinary drinks.
items.cn: 现代英语中，汤力水把这个医学标签带进日常饮品。

note.en: Tonic is the medicine of restoring tension; its family includes tone, tonality, and the opposite atonic.
note.cn: tonic 是「把张力还回去」的药，词族包括 tone、tonality 及其反义形式 atonic。

entries.definition: sound quality or a general quality of feeling
entries.definitionCN: 音色；基调（tonic 去掉 -ic 的名词形式）

entries.definition: the system of keys in music
entries.definitionCN: 调性；音乐调式体系

entries.definition: lacking tone or tension
entries.definitionCN: 无张力的；松弛的（tone 相关，拼写相近但语义相反）

entries.definition: a treatment that cures a problem
entries.definitionCN: 疗法；补救办法（强调治）

entries.definition: a drug that makes the body more active
entries.definitionCN: 兴奋剂；刺激物

entries.definition: a drink or treat that revives you
entries.definitionCN: 提神的东西（口语）

normalIntro.en: Tonic is built on tone: both come from the Greek idea of a stretched string.
normalIntro.cn: tonic 建立在 tone 上：两者都出自希腊语「绷紧的弦」这一意象。

normal.en: Tone and tonic share the Greek root tonos, meaning tension.
normal.cn: tone 与 tonic 共享希腊词根 tonos，意为张力。

normal.en: A tonic water label hides a malaria medicine, quinine.
normal.cn: 汤力水标签背后藏着抗疟药奎宁。

normal.en: In music the tonic is the home note of the key.
normal.cn: 在音乐里，tonic 是调的「家」——主音。

normal.en: The phrase tonic for the spirits shows the verb feel of the word.
normal.cn: 搭配「tonic for the spirits」体现了这个词的鼓励意味。

normal.en: The prefix a- makes atonic, the exact opposite of tonic.
normal.cn: 前缀 a- 构成 atonic，正好是 tonic 的反义。

abstract.en: Picture a slack rope pulled tight by a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一根松垮的绳子被一只手重新拽紧。

abstract.en: Picture a tired face turning bright after a bitter drink.
abstract.cn: 想象一张疲惫的脸喝下苦味饮料后焕发光彩。

abstract.en: Picture a melody landing safely on its first note.
abstract.cn: 想象一段旋律安稳地落回它的第一个音。

examples.en: A brisk walk in the cold air works as a tonic.
examples.cn: 在冷空气里快走一趟就像一剂补药。

examples.en: The singer held the tonic for four bars.
examples.cn: 歌手在主音上持续了四个小节。

examples.en: She ordered a tonic with ice and lemon.
examples.cn: 她点了一杯加冰和柠檬的汤力水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托你可」——托住你、可让你恢复力气，就是补药。这只是谐音联想，与希腊词源无关。

root: 希腊语 tonos（拉紧、张力）→ tonikos（与张力有关的）→ 医学拉丁语 tonicus → 英语 tonic，核心义「把松弛的张力重新拉紧」。

sensesIntro.en: Tonic starts as a medicine that tightens the body, spreads to mood and music, then names a drink and finally acts as an adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: tonic 从把身体重新绷紧的药开始，扩展到心情与音乐，再用来指汤力水，最后用作形容词表示提神。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slack body pulled taut again by a bitter drink.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯苦味药水让人从松垮里重新绷紧。

branches.en: A tonic is the medicine of restored tension.
branches.cn: 补药是把张力还回来的药，是基本义。

branches.en: A cheer works like medicine for the mood.
branches.cn: 振奋心情的东西就像给情绪开的药。

branches.en: The tonic is the tensionless home note of a key.
branches.cn: 主音是一调里无需再拉紧的落脚音。

branches.en: Quinine water keeps the medicinal name of tonic.
branches.cn: 奎宁水沿用了 tonic 的药名。

branches.en: Whether noun or adjective, tonic means giving strength.
branches.cn: 无论是名词还是形容词，tonic 都表示给予力气。

intro.en: Tonic is built from the Greek stem ton-, meaning to stretch, with -ic forming the adjective.
intro.cn: tonic 由希腊词干 ton-（拉伸）构成，词尾 -ic 使其成为形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tonicus was the medical term for relating to tone or tension, borrowed from Greek tonikos.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tonicus 是表示「与张力有关的」医学术语，借自希腊语 tonikos。

items.example: The root ton- gives tone and tension.
items.exampleCN: 词干 ton- 生出 tone 和 tension。

items.example: Tonos is the ancient source word.
items.exampleCN: tonos 是古老源头词。

items.example: The suffix -ic makes tonikos an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 把 tonikos 变成形容词。

items.meaning: a restorative or the key note
items.example: Tonic keeps both medical and musical force.
items.exampleCN: tonic 兼有医学与音乐的双重力量。

items.example: The prefix a- gives atonic, without tension.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 a- 构成 atonic，即没有张力。

items.example: Atonic is used in medicine and grammar.
items.exampleCN: atonic 用于医学和语法。

items.example: The prefix hyper- gives hypertonic.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 hyper- 构成 hypertonic。

items.example: Hypertonic describes stronger salt solutions.
items.exampleCN: hypertonic 描述浓度更高的盐溶液。

items.example: The suffix -ity gives tonicity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 tonicity。

definition_zh: （使）倒下；倾覆；推翻；摇摇欲坠
definition_en: to fall over or to make something fall over, especially something tall or top-heavy
core_image: 一根高而细的木桩被轻轻一推，连根栽倒
scene: 强风吹过，那座摇摇欲坠的旧烟囱终于倒下了。A strong gust finally toppled the rickety old chimney.
sceneCN: 这里 topple 是「倒下、倾倒」（第 1 个义项：高处的东西失去平衡而翻倒）；句意：一阵狂风终于把摇摇欲坠的旧烟囱吹倒了。

derivatives.zh: 被推倒的；倾覆的（过去分词用作形容词）
摇摇欲坠的；即将倾倒的（-ing 分词作形容词）
未被推翻的（un- 否定 + 分词，构词上成立但极少使用）

senses.title: To fall over from being top-heavy
senses.definition: to fall over suddenly, especially because something is tall, unstable, or top-heavy
senses.definitionCN: 突然翻倒，尤因某物高、不稳或头重脚轻
senses.example: The tower toppled in the earthquake.
senses.exampleCN: 那座塔在地震中倒塌了。
senses.why: Top plus the frequentative ending -le suggested a repeated swaying at the top, so the verb first pictures something tall tipping over.
senses.whyCN: top（顶端）加上表反复动作的词尾 -le，本义是顶端来回摇晃，所以动词最初描画的就是高物倾倒。

senses.title: To overthrow a government or leader
senses.definition: to remove a government, ruler, or system from power by force or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 以武力或压力使政府、统治者或制度失去权力
senses.example: Protests toppled the regime within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议活动在几周内就推翻了该政权。
senses.why: If a tall thing can be pushed until it falls, a powerful ruler standing at the top can be pushed down the same way.
senses.whyCN: 既然高的东西能被推到倒塌，站在权力顶端的人也能用同样的方式被推下去。

senses.title: To move unsteadily and almost fall
senses.definition: to walk or move in an unsteady way, as if about to fall
senses.definitionCN: 步履不稳地走或动，好像随时会摔倒
senses.example: He toppled forward on the icy path.
senses.exampleCN: 他在结冰的小路上踉跄着向前扑倒。
senses.why: The same swaying image moves from a still object to a moving body that keeps losing balance.
senses.whyCN: 同一个摇晃意象从静止之物转移到移动的身体上，表现步态不断失衡。

senses.title: To make a record or price collapse
senses.definition: to knock a record or steeply reduce a price or value
senses.definitionCN: 打破纪录，或使价格、价值暴跌
senses.example: Shares toppled after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告发布后股价大幅下挫。
senses.why: Abstract things that stand high, like records and prices, can also be made to fall, so toppling became a metaphor for collapse.
senses.whyCN: 纪录和价格这类「站得高」的抽象事物也能被打落，于是 topple 成了崩落的比喻。

intro.en: Topple is usually taken to come from top plus the frequentative ending -le, though the earliest record only shows the later sense of tumbling.
intro.cn: 一般认为 topple 来自 top（顶端）加表反复的词尾 -le；早期文献只见「翻滚」义，构词细节仍存推测。

items.en: Topple appears meaning to tumble or roll over.
items.cn: 十六世纪 topple 出现，意为翻滚、跌倒。

items.en: The sense shifts to falling headfirst from a height.
items.cn: 十七世纪词义转向从高处头朝下栽落。

items.en: Most sources link it to top plus -le, seen as a repeated swaying.
items.cn: 多数来源把它分析为 top 加 -le，视作反复摇晃。

items.en: Topple comes to mean overthrow a ruler or state.
items.cn: 十八世纪 topple 开始表示推翻统治者或国家。

items.en: Modern usage extends to records, prices, and leaders.
items.cn: 现代用法扩展到纪录、价格与领导人。

note.en: Topple describes a tall thing losing balance; tumble, collapse, and overthrow sit closest to it.
note.cn: topple 描述高物失衡倒下，tumble、collapse 与 overthrow 与它最贴近。

entries.definition: the highest part of something
entries.definitionCN: 顶端（一般认为 topple 由它派生）

entries.definition: to drink alcohol regularly
entries.definitionCN: 常喝酒；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to walk with short unsteady steps
entries.definitionCN: 蹒跚学步；只是拼写相近，词源不确定

entries.definition: to fall suddenly and helplessly
entries.definitionCN: 翻滚；摔倒

entries.definition: to fall down as a whole structure
entries.definitionCN: 倒塌；崩溃

entries.definition: to remove a government by force
entries.definitionCN: 推翻（政权）

normalIntro.en: Topple is top in motion: the tallest part loses its balance and comes down.
normalIntro.cn: topple 就是 top 在动：最高处失去平衡，砸了下来。

normal.en: Top plus -le makes a small verb about a tall thing swaying.
normal.cn: top 加 -le，构成一个描述高物摇晃的短动词。

normal.en: Topple over is the everyday phrase for a fall.
normal.cn: topple over 是表示「翻倒」的常用说法。

normal.en: Do not confuse topple with tipple, which means drinking.
normal.cn: 别把 topple 和表示喝酒的 tipple 弄混。

normal.en: The verb works for both things and people in power.
normal.cn: 这个词既能用于物体，也能用于掌权者。

normal.en: Its history moves from tumbling to falling to overthrowing.
normal.cn: 它的词义从翻滚走到跌倒，再到推翻。

abstract.en: Picture a domino standing on one narrow edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张骨牌用很窄的边立着。

abstract.en: Picture a crown rolling down a flight of steps.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠顺着台阶往下滚。

abstract.en: Picture a stock chart plunging off its highest point.
abstract.cn: 想象一张股价图从最高点直落下来。

examples.en: The wind toppled the empty bins in the yard.
examples.cn: 风把院子里的空垃圾桶吹翻了。

examples.en: A single scandal toppled the minister within days.
examples.cn: 一桩丑闻几天内就把这位大臣拉下了台。

examples.en: The vase toppled off the shelf.
examples.cn: 花瓶从架子上翻落了下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「top 了」——顶端的东西失去了平衡，就倒下了。这是拆词联想，并非严格词源。

root: 一般认为由英语 top（顶端）加表反复动作的词尾 -le 构成：顶上反复摇晃，终至倒下；早期文献中的构词细节仍属推测。

sensesIntro.en: Topple begins with a tall thing falling, extends to rulers pushed down and bodies stumbling, and finally to anything standing high that collapses.
sensesIntro.cn: topple 从高物倒下开始，扩展到被推倒的统治者与踉跄的身体，最后用于任何站得高的抽象事物崩落。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tall post nudged once and going down whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根高高的木桩被推了一下，整根栽倒。

branches.en: Physical tipping over is the root sense.
branches.cn: 物体物理上的倾倒是最根本的义项。

branches.en: Power, like a tall structure, can be pushed down.
branches.cn: 权力像高耸的建筑，也能被推倒。

branches.en: A stumbling body keeps repeating the near fall.
branches.cn: 踉跄的身体不断重复近乎倒下的动作。

branches.en: Records and prices stand high before they crash.
branches.cn: 纪录与价格先站得高，随后才崩落。

branches.en: All three describe a high point giving way.
branches.cn: 三者都描述一个高点让位下坠。

intro.en: Topple is a short English verb usually analysed as top plus -le, with no Latin origin.
intro.cn: topple 是简短的英语动词，一般分析为 top 加 -le，没有拉丁语来源。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor is recorded for topple, so the Latin side stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: topple 没有可考的拉丁语祖先，因此拉丁同源部分留空。

items.example: Top is the likely building block of topple.
items.exampleCN: top 可能是 topple 的构词成分。

items.example: The suffix -le marks repeated swaying.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -le 标志反复摇晃。

items.example: Topple pictures a tall thing falling.
items.exampleCN: topple 描画高物倒下。

items.example: Toppled is used for past events.
items.exampleCN: toppled 用于过去事件。

items.example: Toppling can act as a noun.
items.exampleCN: toppling 可以作名词。

items.meaning: to sway on the edge of falling
items.example: Teeter describes the moment before toppling.
items.exampleCN: teeter 描述倒下前的那一瞬。

items.meaning: rarely used form not to be relied on
items.meaningCN: 极少使用的形式，不宜套用
items.example: Avoid building new words on it.
items.exampleCN: 不宜以此类推造词。

items.example: Overthrow overlaps with the political sense.
items.exampleCN: overthrow 与政治义项重叠。

definition_zh: 折磨；痛苦；煎熬；使痛苦；烦扰
definition_en: great suffering of mind or body, or the act of causing such suffering
core_image: 一架绞绳机把绳子一点点绞紧，痛得人无法安宁
scene: 伤口迟迟不愈，夜里的疼痛让他整宿无法入睡。The unhealed wound was a torment that kept him awake all night.
sceneCN: 这里 torment 是「折磨、煎熬」（第 1 个义项：身心遭受的剧痛与煎熬，作名词）；句意：未愈合的伤口是一种让他整夜难眠的折磨。

derivatives.zh: 备受折磨的（torment 加 -ed）
令人痛苦的；折磨人的（torment 加 -ing）
折磨者（torment + -or 表施动者）

senses.title: Great suffering of mind or body
senses.definition: severe pain or suffering, especially of the mind
senses.definitionCN: 剧烈的痛苦或煎熬，尤指精神上的
senses.example: The years of exile were pure torment to her.
senses.exampleCN: 流亡的那些年对她纯粹是折磨。
senses.why: Latin tormentum first meant a twisted rope used to hurl a stone, so the noun carried the strain of something wound tight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tormentum 本指投石用的绞紧绳索，所以名词从一开始就带着被绞紧、绷到极限的紧张感。

senses.title: Something that causes pain
senses.titleCN: 折磨人的事物；痛苦之源
senses.definition: a person or thing that causes great pain or worry
senses.definitionCN: 造成巨大痛苦或忧虑的人或事物
senses.example: That tooth is a constant torment.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗牙一直折磨人。
senses.why: The word for the feeling also names the cause, just as a wound both hurts and is a torment.
senses.whyCN: 表示感受的词也用来指源头，就像伤口既是疼痛本身，也是一种折磨。

senses.title: To cause someone great pain
senses.definition: to make someone suffer intense pain or anxiety
senses.definitionCN: 使某人承受剧烈疼痛或焦虑
senses.example: Memories of the accident tormented him for years.
senses.exampleCN: 事故的回忆折磨了他多年。
senses.why: Turning the noun into a verb keeps the image of a rope being wound tighter and tighter around someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词后，仍保留绳子在某人身上越绞越紧的画面。

senses.title: To pester someone persistently
senses.definition: to annoy or badger someone repeatedly, often with small requests
senses.definitionCN: 反复惹烦或纠缠某人，常为小请求
senses.example: Stop tormenting your sister with that song.
senses.exampleCN: 别再拿那首歌烦你姐姐了。
senses.why: The agony of a wound softened into the lighter annoyance of steady nagging.
senses.whyCN: 剧烈的痛苦被弱化成持续唠叨带来的轻微烦躁。

intro.en: Torment comes from Latin tormentum, a machine for hurling stones, later a torture device, built on torquere, to twist.
intro.cn: torment 来自拉丁语 tormentum（投石器，后指刑具），源自 torquere（扭绞）。

items.en: Torquere means to twist or turn.
items.cn: torquere 意为扭绞、转动。

items.en: Tormentum names the twisted rope of a siege engine.
items.cn: tormentum 指攻城器械上绞紧的绳索。

items.en: The same word comes to mean a device or act of torture.
items.cn: 后来同一个词转为指刑具或施刑。

items.en: Old French torment carries both the pain and the device.
items.cn: 古法语 torment 兼指痛苦与刑具。

items.en: English torment begins as bodily torture.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 torment 先指肉体酷刑。

items.en: The verb form and the milder sense of pestering develop.
items.cn: 其后发展出动词形式与较轻的「烦扰」义。

note.en: Torment sits between torture, agony, and the milder annoyance of pestering; its root torquere gives torture and distort.
note.cn: torment 处于 torture、agony 与较轻的「烦扰」之间，词根 torquere 则导出 torture、distort。

entries.definition: the inflicting of severe pain
entries.definitionCN: 酷刑；折磨（同源于 torquere）

entries.definition: to twist something out of shape
entries.definitionCN: 使扭曲（dis- + torquere）

entries.definition: a turning force
entries.definitionCN: 扭矩；转动力

entries.definition: extreme pain of body or mind
entries.definitionCN: 极大痛苦；煎熬

entries.definition: pain experienced over time
entries.definitionCN: 苦难；痛苦经历

entries.definition: to trouble someone repeatedly
entries.definitionCN: 反复骚扰（接近较轻的烦扰义）

normalIntro.en: Torment is the twist of torquere: something wound so tight that it hurts.
normalIntro.cn: torment 就是 torquere 的「扭」：绞得太紧，于是疼。

normal.en: Torment shares its root with torture and distortion.
normal.cn: torment 与 torture、distortion 同根。

normal.en: In torment is the standard phrase for being in pain.
normal.cn: in torment 是表示「处于痛苦中」的固定说法。

normal.en: Actor and action share a form: the noun is torments too.
normal.cn: 名词复数与动词三单同形，都是 torments。

normal.en: The -or ending builds tormentor, the one who torments.
normal.cn: 加 -or 构成 tormentor，指施加折磨的人。

normal.en: The old stone-hurling engine explains the original strain.
normal.cn: 古代的投石机解释了原初那种绷紧的紧张感。

abstract.en: Picture a rope wound around a post until it creaks.
abstract.cn: 想象麻绳缠在柱子上，一直扭到咯吱作响。

abstract.en: Picture a mind circling one thought all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头整夜在心里打转。

abstract.en: Picture a small voice nagging without a break.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不停唠叨的小声音。

examples.en: She endured months of torment after the diagnosis.
examples.cn: 确诊之后，她忍受了数月的折磨。

examples.en: He was tormented by doubts before the vote.
examples.cn: 投票之前，他被疑虑折磨着。

examples.en: The children tormented the cat until it ran away.
examples.cn: 孩子们一直烦扰那只猫，直到它跑掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托着没停」——痛苦一直托着你不放，就是折磨。这只是谐音联想，与拉丁词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 torquere（扭绞）→ tormentum（投石机的绞绳，后指刑具）→ 古法语 torment → 英语 torment，核心义「被绞紧到痛苦」。

sensesIntro.en: Torment moves from a tight-wound torture device to the pain it causes, then to the cause itself, to the verb of inflicting pain, and finally to mild pestering.
sensesIntro.cn: torment 从绞紧的刑具走到它造成的痛苦，再指痛苦的源头、施加痛苦的动词，最后弱化为轻微的烦扰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope twisted tighter and tighter until someone cries out.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳索越绞越紧，人终于痛得叫出声。

branches.en: The pain itself is the everyday noun sense.
branches.cn: 痛苦本身是最日常的名词义项。

branches.en: A thing that hurts stands for the hurting.
branches.cn: 让人疼的事物转指疼痛本身。

branches.en: The verb keeps the image of winding someone tight.
branches.cn: 动词保留把人越绞越紧的意象。

branches.en: The edge softens into steady nagging.
branches.cn: 锋利的痛苦弱化为持续的唠叨。

branches.en: Feeling and inflicting share one form.
branches.cn: 感受与施加共用同一个词形。

intro.en: Torment is built on the Latin root torqu-, to twist, with the noun ending -ment.
intro.cn: torment 由拉丁词根 torqu-（扭绞）与名词词尾 -ment 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin torquere means to twist, and tormentum is the twisted engine or torture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 torquere 意为扭绞，tormentum 指绞紧的器械或刑具。

items.example: The root torqu- gives torque and distort.
items.exampleCN: 词根 torqu- 生出 torque 和 distort。

items.example: Torquere is the source verb.
items.exampleCN: torquere 是源头动词。

items.example: The suffix -ment forms tormentum.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 tormentum。

items.example: Tormentum first named the twisted rope of a catapult.
items.exampleCN: tormentum 最初指投石机绞紧的绳。

items.meaning: great pain or to cause pain
items.example: Torment keeps the medical-legal weight.
items.exampleCN: torment 保留了沉重的意味。

items.example: The suffix -or gives tormentor.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 tormentor。

items.example: Tormentor is the agent noun.
items.exampleCN: tormentor 是施动名词。

items.example: Tormenting describes what causes pain.
items.exampleCN: tormenting 形容造成痛苦之物。

items.example: Torture shares the twisting root.
items.exampleCN: torture 同享「扭绞」词根。

definition_zh: 麻木；迟钝；迟钝状态；（动物）休眠；麻木状态
definition_en: a state of physical or mental inactivity; a dull, sluggish condition, including the dormant rest of animals
core_image: 冬眠的青蛙缩成一团，四肢僵硬，连敌人靠近也不想动
scene: 冬天暴风雪过去后，人们在池塘边掀开一块石头，发现下面有一只缩成一团的青蛙。After the winter blizzard, a frog under the pond stone stayed in torpor and hardly moved at all.
sceneCN: 这里 torpor 是「休眠状态」（第 1 个义项：动物因寒冷或食物短缺而进入的缓慢休息状态）；句意：冬天暴风雪过后，人们在池塘边掀开一块石头，发现下面有一只缩成一团的青蛙，它处于麻木缓慢的状态，几乎一动不动。

derivatives.zh: torpor 加形容词后缀 -id 构成，义为「麻木的；迟钝的；休眠的」
torpid 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「麻木；迟钝」
torpid 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「麻木地；迟钝地」
torpid 加名词后缀 -tude 构成，义为「麻木状态」，属罕用词

senses.title: The dormant state of an animal
senses.definition: the state of reduced activity and very low body temperature into which some animals enter during cold or dry seasons
senses.definitionCN: 某些动物在寒冷或干旱季节进入的活动减少、体温很低的休息状态
senses.example: Frogs fall into torpor when the pond freezes.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘结冰时，青蛙会进入休眠状态。
senses.why: The Latin noun torpor originally means numbness, and a numb, motionless body is exactly what a hibernating animal shows: activity is switched off before breathing and warmth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 torpor 本义就是「麻木」，而麻木而不动的身子正好像冬眠的动物：呼吸和温度还在，活动却先被关掉了。

senses.title: Sluggishness of body
senses.definition: a slow, heavy condition of the body in which movement feels difficult
senses.definitionCN: 身体沉重缓慢、动起来很费力的状态
senses.example: Heat and heavy food left the workers in a dull torpor.
senses.exampleCN: 闷热和油腻的饭菜让工人们昏昏沉沉的。
senses.why: From numbness came the everyday sense of a body that feels too heavy to move, as if its limbs had gone stiff.
senses.whyCN: 从「麻木」引申出日常义：身子沉得以至于不想动，四肢好像都僵住了。

senses.title: Sluggishness of mind
senses.definition: a dull state of mind in which thinking or interest is slow and hard to stir
senses.definitionCN: 思维或兴趣缓慢、难以被激起的呆滞心理状态
senses.example: Long weeks without reading brought on a torpor of the mind.
senses.exampleCN: 好几周不读书，让人头脑一片呆滞。
senses.why: The same numbness is transferred from limbs to thought: a stiff mind does not grip ideas, just as stiff limbs do not move.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「麻木」从四肢转到思维：僵硬的脑子抓不住念头，就像僵硬的四肢动不了。

senses.title: Unwillingness to act
senses.definition: a lazy or careless refusal to act, often shared by a group or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 懒惰或漫不经心地不愿行动，常指群体或机构的状况
senses.example: The committee sank into torpor and let the plan die.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会变得懒散，使这项计划无声无息地夭折了。
senses.why: When inactivity is chosen rather than imposed by cold, the numb state becomes blameworthy slackness that freezes a whole group.
senses.whyCN: 当不活动不是寒冷造成的，而是自己选择的，这种麻木就成了该受责备的懒散，会把整个群体都冻结住。

senses.title: A lull in activity
senses.definition: a quiet period in which the usual activity of a place or process slows almost to a stop
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方或过程原本的活动几乎停下来的安静时期
senses.example: After the harvest, a brief torpor settled over the village.
senses.exampleCN: 秋收过后，村子安静下来，陷入短暂的沉寂。
senses.why: The noun can also name the pause itself, so something that is alive but still can be said to lie in torpor.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也可以指停顿本身，所以一个仍然活着但没有动静的事物，也可以说处于 torpor 之中。

intro.en: Torpor comes from Latin torpor, numbness or sluggishness, formed from torpere, to be stiff or numb.
intro.cn: torpor 来自拉丁语 torpor（麻木、迟钝），由 torpere（僵硬、麻木）构成。

items.en: The verb torpere means to be stiff, numb, or stunned.
items.cn: 动词 torpere 意为僵硬、麻木、发呆。

items.en: The noun torpor means numbness or sluggishness of body or mind.
items.cn: 名词 torpor 意为身体或心智的麻木、迟钝。

items.en: Writers use the word for the dull rest of winter in living things.
items.cn: 古典作家用它描述生物在冬天的迟钝休眠。

items.en: English borrows the noun directly from Latin for a dull, numb state.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入这个名词，表示昏沉麻木。

items.en: Biology adopts the word for the dormancy of animals such as frogs.
items.cn: 十九世纪生物学把该词用于青蛙等动物的休眠。

items.en: Modern usage keeps both the human and the animal senses side by side.
items.cn: 现代用法同时保留人的迟钝与动物的休眠两种含义。

note.en: Torpor is the noun for a numb, motionless state, next to its own family in torpid, and beside words for rest or sleep.
note.cn: torpor 是表示「麻木不动」的名词，与同族的 torpid 相邻，也与「休息、睡眠」类词接近。

entries.definition: numb, sluggish, or dormant
entries.definitionCN: 麻木的；迟钝的；休眠的

entries.definition: the quality of being torpid
entries.definitionCN: 迟钝；麻木性

entries.definition: only slightly warm
entries.definitionCN: 微温的；不冷不热（只是拼写与 torpid 相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a lack of energy and enthusiasm
entries.definitionCN: 无精打采；倦怠

entries.definition: a slow and heavy manner of moving
entries.definitionCN: 迟缓；迟钝

entries.definition: a resting state in which growth or activity stops
entries.definitionCN: 休眠；蛰伏

normalIntro.en: Torpor is a cold, stiff state: the body has gone numb and slow, as if it had turned to wood.
normalIntro.cn: torpor 是一种又冷又僵的状态：身体麻木迟缓，好像变成了木头。

normal.en: The adjective torpid keeps the same idea, so a torpid animal lies in torpor.
normal.cn: 形容词 torpid 保留同一个意思，所以说一只 torpid 的动物正处于 torpor 之中。

normal.en: In torpor describes being in an inactive state, not just feeling tired.
normal.cn: in torpor 描述的是处于不活动的状态，而不只是觉得累。

normal.en: Fall into torpor is the phrase used for entering dormancy.
normal.cn: fall into torpor 是表示进入休眠的固定说法。

normal.en: Compare lethargy for lack of energy and torpor for numbness plus stillness.
normal.cn: 对比 lethargy（缺精力）与 torpor（麻木且静止）。

normal.en: Mind torpor is used in books about dullness of thought.
normal.cn: torpor of the mind 常见于谈论思维迟钝的文字。

abstract.en: Picture a frog wrapped in frost, not sleeping but switched off.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被霜裹住的青蛙，不是睡着，而是像被关掉了开关。

abstract.en: Feel your legs after hours in one position, heavy and stiff.
abstract.cn: 回想久坐之后腿的沉重僵硬。

abstract.en: Imagine an eye that looks but does not focus.
abstract.cn: 想象一只睁着却没有聚焦的眼睛。

examples.en: Many reptiles survive cold winters in torpor.
examples.cn: 许多爬行动物在麻木休眠中熬过寒冷的冬天。

examples.en: The long holiday ended in a pleasant torpor for the whole family.
examples.cn: 长假结束时，全家都处于一种惬意的慵懒状态。

examples.en: A month without new tasks left the team in mental torpor.
examples.cn: 一个月没有新任务，团队陷入了迟钝懒散。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托婆」——托着婆婆晒太阳，两人都懒洋洋地不想动；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 torpere（僵硬、麻木）→ torpor（麻木、迟钝）→ 英语 torpor，核心义「身体和心智都僵住不动」。同族形容词为 torpid（麻木的）。

sensesIntro.en: Torpor starts from the numbness of a dormant body and spreads to sluggish limbs, a dull mind, unwillingness to act, and finally any quiet lull.
sensesIntro.cn: torpor 从动物休眠时的麻木开始，扩展到迟滞的四肢、呆滞的头脑、不愿行动，最后泛指一切活动的停顿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frog frozen stiff under a stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头下面冻得僵硬的青蛙。

branches.en: The numb body of a dormant animal is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 休眠动物麻木的身体是最早的义项。

branches.en: Heavy, slow limbs are the everyday body sense.
branches.cn: 沉重缓慢的四肢是日常的身体义项。

branches.en: A dull mind lets the numb image move into thought.
branches.cn: 呆滞的头脑让麻木的画面转入思维领域。

branches.en: Inaction by choice and a quiet lull are the social senses.
branches.cn: 自愿的懒散与安静的停顿是社会层面的义项。

branches.en: Both the frozen frog and the silent village are alive but still.
branches.cn: 冻住的青蛙与沉寂的村子都活着却静止不动。

intro.en: Torpor is an untouched Latin noun, and English builds torpid, torpidity, and torpidly on its stem.
intro.cn: torpor 是原样借来的拉丁语名词，英语在它的词干上构成 torpid、torpidity 和 torpidly。

latinIntro.en: Latin torpere means to be stiff or numb, and torpor means a numb state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 torpere 意为僵硬、麻木，照此构成的 torpor 意为麻木状态。

items.example: Torpere gives the stiff image.
items.exampleCN: torpere 提供僵直的意象。

items.example: Torpor is the source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: torpor 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: English keeps the noun unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 英语名词保持原拼写不变。

items.example: Torpid adds a Latin adjective ending to the stem.
items.exampleCN: torpid 在词干后加拉丁语形容词词尾。

items.example: The suffix -id forms torpid.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -id 构成 torpid。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms torpidity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 torpidity。

items.example: Torpidity means the state of being torpid.
items.exampleCN: torpidity 指迟钝麻木的状态。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms torpidly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 torpidly。

items.example: The suffix -tude forms the rare torpitude.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tude 构成罕用词 torpitude。

definition_zh: 激流；洪流；倾注；（言语、情感等的）连发；大量
definition_en: a fast, violent stream of water, and by extension a great rush of words, feeling, or anything else that pours out
core_image: 山洪裹着碎石从峡谷轰然冲下，水声震耳
scene: 暴雨过后，山上的水顺着峡谷冲下来，把路边的小路整个盖住了。After the storm, a roaring torrent poured down the canyon and swept the trail away.
sceneCN: 这里 torrent 是「激流、洪流」（第 1 个义项：水势湍急、力量巨大的水流）；句意：暴雨过后，山上冲下的激流带着轰响灌进峡谷，把小路冲毁了。

derivatives.zh: torrent 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为「暴雨般的；湍急的」
torrential 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「如激流般倾泻地」

senses.title: A violent stream of water
senses.definition: a fast and powerful stream of water that rushes down a channel or a slope
senses.definitionCN: 在河道或坡面上急速奔流、力量巨大的水流
senses.example: The torrent cut a new channel through the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 激流在山坡上冲出一条新的水道。
senses.why: The Latin source torrens describes water that is boiling or roaring, so the noun keeps the picture of a stream that seethes with force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 torrens 描述的是沸腾、咆哮的水，所以这个名词保留了「水在用力翻涌」的画面。

senses.title: Heavy, pouring rain
senses.definition: rain that falls in sudden, very dense sheets
senses.definitionCN: 来势突然、极为密集的降雨
senses.example: Rain fell in torrents all through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨倾盆地下了一整夜。
senses.why: Rain so heavy that it looks like a stream falling from the sky borrows the water image directly.
senses.whyCN: 雨大到看起来像天上倒下来的一道水，自然就借用了「激流」这一水景。

senses.title: A flood of words
senses.definition: a very large number of words spoken or written without a pause
senses.definitionCN: 不加停顿地说出或写下的极大数量的话语
senses.example: She answered with a torrent of complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 她回敬了一连串的抱怨。
senses.why: Speech pours out with the same force and direction as water, so an unstoppable rush of words is called a torrent.
senses.whyCN: 话语和水一样有方向和冲力，一旦停不下来，就被称为一股 torrent。

senses.title: A rush of feeling
senses.definition: an overwhelming rush of strong emotion or protest
senses.definitionCN: 强烈情感或抗议势力汹涌而来、难以阻挡
senses.example: A torrent of protest met the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 新税引来一片汹涌的抗议。
senses.why: Emotion that cannot be stopped behaves like flood water, so the same word covers a surge of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 无法遏止的情感像洪水一样，于是同一个词也用来形容情感的涌动。

senses.title: A very large amount
senses.definition: a very large and continuous supply of things of any kind
senses.definitionCN: 任何事物大量而不间断地涌来
senses.example: A torrent of data floods the new system every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 每小时都有大量数据涌进新系统。
senses.why: The image of water pouring in is stretched to data, goods, and messages, which all arrive in floods.
senses.whyCN: 「水涌进来」的画面被延伸到数据、货物和信息，它们同样是一股股涌来的。

intro.en: Torrent comes from French torrent, from Latin torrens, boiling or rushing water, from torrere, to burn or scorch.
intro.cn: torrent 经法语 torrent 传入，源自拉丁语 torrens（沸腾、奔涌的水），后者来自 torrere（燃烧、灼烧）。

items.en: The verb torrere means to burn, roast, or scorch.
items.cn: 动词 torrere 意为燃烧、烤、灼烧。

items.en: The adjective and noun torrens describes water that seethes or rushes like boiling liquid.
items.cn: 形容词兼名词 torrens 描述像沸水一样翻涌急冲的水。

items.en: The form torrent names a rushing stream in French.
items.cn: 法语形式 torrent 用来指奔涌的溪流。

items.en: English borrows torrent for a violent stream of water.
items.cn: 英语借入 torrent，表示湍急的水流。

items.en: The word is extended figuratively to words and feelings that pour out.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，该词引申形容倾泻而出的话语与情感。

items.en: Modern use adds the computing sense of a torrent of data.
items.cn: 现代用法又加上「数据洪流」等信息类义项。

note.en: Torrent is the noun for a roaring rush, built on its own adjective torrential and standing beside stream and flood.
note.cn: torrent 是表示「轰然奔涌」的名词，其形容词 torrential 与它同族，同时与 stream、flood 等词相邻。

entries.definition: like a torrent, very heavy
entries.definitionCN: 激流般的；暴雨似的

entries.definition: very hot and dry
entries.definitionCN: 酷热的；炎热的（与 torrent 同出 torrere）

entries.definition: a flow of water or air
entries.definitionCN: 水流；气流（只是与 torrent 词形相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a small river or a steady flow
entries.definitionCN: 小溪；流动

entries.definition: a great overflow of water
entries.definitionCN: 洪水；泛滥

entries.definition: a small waterfall or a rushing fall
entries.definitionCN: 小瀑布；倾泻

normalIntro.en: Torrent is water that boils over a slope: hot, fast, and impossible to stand against.
normalIntro.cn: torrent 是顺坡翻涌的水：又猛又快，挡也挡不住。

normal.en: The adjective torrential describes rain that comes in torrents.
normal.cn: 形容词 torrential 描述像 torrent 一样倒下来的雨。

normal.en: A torrent of abuse means a flood of angry words.
normal.cn: a torrent of abuse 指劈头盖脸的怒骂。

normal.en: In torrents tells you it rains very heavily.
normal.cn: in torrents 说明雨下得非常大。

normal.en: The root torrere means to burn, which explains the picture of seething water.
normal.cn: 词根 torrere 意为燃烧，这解释了「水在翻沸」的画面。

normal.en: Compare stream for a gentle flow and torrent for a violent rush.
normal.cn: 对比 stream（平缓的水流）与 torrent（猛烈的水流）。

abstract.en: Hear the roar of a mountain flood hitting the rocks.
abstract.cn: 听山中洪水撞上岩石时的轰鸣声。

abstract.en: Picture a dam gate opening all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一道蓄水闸门被一次全部打开。

abstract.en: See a speaker whose words pour out faster than you can follow.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人说话快得你跟不上。

examples.en: The road was blocked by a torrent that had come down from the hills.
examples.cn: 从山上冲下的一股激流把路堵住了。

examples.en: His new book drew a torrent of praise.
examples.cn: 他的新书引来一片如潮的赞誉。

examples.en: The pipes burst and released a torrent of hot water.
examples.cn: 管子破裂，涌出一股热水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「秃伦特」——水流太猛，把岸边的树都冲秃了，只剩秃秃的河床；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 torrere（燃烧、沸腾）→ torrens（沸腾奔涌的水）→ 古法语 torrent → 英语 torrent，核心义「像沸水一样猛烈奔涌」。同族形容词 torrential（暴雨般的）、torrid（酷热的）。

sensesIntro.en: Torrent starts as rushing water, yields heavy rain, and then lets the pouring image carry over to words, feeling, and any great inflow.
sensesIntro.cn: torrent 首先是奔涌的水，其次是倾盆的雨，再让「倾泻」的画面延伸到话语、情感和一切大量涌入之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: flood water roaring down a canyon.
core.cn: 核心意象：洪水在峡谷中轰鸣而下。

branches.en: A violent stream of water is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 猛烈的水流是字面义项。

branches.en: Walls of rain are the weather sense of the same water image.
branches.cn: 倾盆大雨是同一种水景的天气义项。

branches.en: Words that pour out take the water image into speech.
branches.cn: 倾泻而出的话语把水景带入言语领域。

branches.en: Emotion and sheer quantity are the extended senses.
branches.cn: 情感与大量是扩展出来的义项。

branches.en: A mountain torrent and a wall of rain both arrive as force.
branches.cn: 山间激流和倾盆大雨都以一股力量降临。

intro.en: Torrent is a Latin particle of the verb torrere, and English builds torrential and torrentially on its stem.
intro.cn: torrent 源自拉丁语动词 torrere，英语在它的词干上构成 torrential 与 torrentially。

latinIntro.en: Latin torrens means burning or boiling, and is used for water that boils over the rocks.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 torrens 意为燃烧、沸腾，用来形容在岩石间翻沸的水。

items.example: Torrere gives the heat image behind torrent.
items.exampleCN: torrere 提供 torrent 背后「热」的意象。

items.example: Torrens is used of a rushing stream.
items.exampleCN: torrens 用来形容奔涌的溪流。

items.example: French torrent keeps the water sense.
items.exampleCN: 法语 torrent 保留水流之义。

items.example: English keeps the noun shape.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留名词原形。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms torrential.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 构成 torrential。

items.example: Torrential rain flooded the street.
items.exampleCN: torrential rain 指暴雨。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms torrentially.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 torrentially。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms torrid from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 参与构成同根词 torrid。

items.example: Torrid shares the root meaning to burn.
items.exampleCN: torrid 共享「燃烧」词根。

definition_zh: 陆龟；（引申）行动迟缓的人
definition_en: a slow land animal with a hard shell on its back and belly, and by extension a person who moves very slowly
core_image: 一只背着厚重硬壳的陆龟，一步一步在干热的沙地上慢慢挪动
scene: 沙漠动物园里，饲养员把一片生菜放在沙地上，一只陆龟花了很长时间才爬过去。At the desert zoo, a tortoise took nearly an hour to cross the sand and reach the lettuce.
sceneCN: 这里 tortoise 是「陆龟」（第 1 个义项：生活在陆地上、背着硬壳的行动缓慢的爬行动物）；句意：在沙漠动物园里，一只陆龟花了将近一个小时才穿过沙地，够到那片生菜。

derivatives.zh: tortoise 加 shell（壳）构成的复合词，义为「龟甲；玳瑁」
复合词作形容词，义为「龟甲色的；玳瑁色的」

senses.title: The slow shelled land reptile
senses.definition: a reptile of the family Testudinidae that lives on land and carries a heavy domed shell
senses.definitionCN: 陆龟科的一种爬行动物，生活在陆地上，背着厚重的穹顶状壳
senses.example: A giant tortoise can live for more than a hundred years.
senses.exampleCN: 一只巨型陆龟能活一百多年。
senses.why: The animal takes its English name from the Old French and Latin forms, but the picture behind the word is simply the hard domed shell that carries the body and is the creatures whole shelter.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物的英语名来自古法语和拉丁语形式，而这个词背后的画面就是那副把身子装在里面、同时也是整个庇护所的穹顶硬壳。

senses.title: A very slow mover
senses.definition: a person, often a driver or a worker, who moves far more slowly than everyone else
senses.definitionCN: 常指司机或工人，行动比别人慢得多的人
senses.example: Come on, tortoise, the traffic light will change soon.
senses.exampleCN: 快点吧，慢乌龟，绿灯马上要变了。
senses.why: Because the animal is proverbial for slowness, the noun becomes a gentle or teasing label for anyone who crawls along.
senses.whyCN: 因为陆龟在习语里就是「慢」的代名词，这个名词就成了形容一切拖着走的人的宛转或打趣的称呼。

senses.title: The shell or its material
senses.definition: the hard covering of the animal, or the mottled material worked from the shell of sea turtles
senses.definitionCN: 该动物的坚硬外壳，或由海龟壳加工成的斑驳材料
senses.example: The comb was made of polished tortoise shell.
senses.exampleCN: 那把梳子是用打磨过的龟甲做的。
senses.why: Naming the animal came to name the shell itself, and the shell in turn named an inlaid material, though strictly that material comes from the hawksbill turtle.
senses.whyCN: 用动物名指其壳，再由壳指一种镶嵌材料；不过严格说，那种材料其实来自玳瑁海龟。

senses.title: Steady patience in a race
senses.definition: the person or attitude that wins slowly and steadily rather than by speed
senses.definitionCN: 那类靠缓慢稳定、而非靠速度取胜的参赛者或态度
senses.example: Her firm was a tortoise in a market full of hares.
senses.exampleCN: 在一个尽是兔子的市场里，她的公司就是那只稳扎稳打的乌龟。
senses.why: The old fable of the tortoise and the hare turns the slow animal into a symbol of patient, persistent effort.
senses.whyCN: 龟兔赛跑的古老寓言把这只慢动物变成了耐心与坚持的象征。

senses.title: A firm, protective attitude
senses.definition: a defensive withdrawal into a shell of stubborn caution through which others cannot easily reach
senses.definitionCN: 像缩进龟壳一样固执地自我封闭、别人难以触及的防备姿态
senses.example: When asked about money, she pulled into her shell like a tortoise.
senses.exampleCN: 一问到钱，她就像乌龟一样缩进壳里。
senses.why: The shell that protects the body also supplies the image of a person withdrawing into an unapproachable, hard exterior.
senses.whyCN: 保护身体的壳也提供了「缩进不可接近的硬外壳」这一形象。

intro.en: Tortoise descends from Medieval Latin tortuca, of debated origin, and was reshaped in English under French spelling; the Greek tartoukhos is a separate but similar-looking word.
intro.cn: tortoise 源于中世纪拉丁语 tortuca，其来源尚存争议，在英语中受法语拼写影响改形；希腊语 tartoukhos 是另一个外形相近但来源不同的词。

items.en: The usual Latin word for a tortoise is testudo, from testa, a shell or tile.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语称陆龟为 testudo，源于 testa（壳、瓦片）。

items.en: Vulgar Latin retains a form tortuca, whose further origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语保留了 tortuca 这一形式，其更早的来源尚不确定。

items.en: French tortue and similar forms pass the animal name across the Channel.
items.cn: 法语 tortue 等形式把这个动物名传到英吉利海峡彼岸。

items.en: English writes tortuce or tortuse, later reshaped to tortoise.
items.cn: 英语写作 tortuce 或 tortuse，后来改拼为 tortoise。

items.en: Writers sometimes connect the word wrongly with Latin tortus, twisted, which is a folk link, not the true source.
items.cn: 十六世纪有些作者误把该词与拉丁语 tortus（扭曲）相联系，这属于民间推测，并非真实来源。

items.en: Modern English keeps tortoise for the land animal, and turtle is now used for species living in water.
items.cn: 现代英语用 tortoise 指陆生种类，水生种类则多说 turtle。

note.en: Tortoise is the shelled land reptile and the byword for slowness, close to turtle and terrapin and to words for a slow pace.
note.cn: tortoise 指背壳的陆生爬行动物，也是「慢」的代名词，与 turtle、terrapin 以及表示缓慢的词相邻。

entries.definition: causing great pain
entries.definitionCN: 折磨人的；痛苦的（只是拼写与 tortoise 相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the shell of the animal or a mottled material
entries.definitionCN: 龟甲；玳瑁；龟甲花纹的

entries.definition: full of twists and turns
entries.definitionCN: 曲折的；弯弯绕绕的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a reptile with a shell that lives in water or on land
entries.definitionCN: 海龟；水龟

entries.definition: a small turtle living in fresh or brackish water
entries.definitionCN: 淡水龟；泥龟

entries.definition: a small soft animal with a coiled shell that crawls very slowly
entries.definitionCN: 蜗牛；行动极慢的动物

normalIntro.en: Tortoise names the shelled land creature, and the slow shell is the whole word: hard outside, patient inside.
normalIntro.cn: tortoise 指背壳的陆生动物，整个词就是那副慢吞吞的硬壳：外面坚硬，里面耐心。

normal.en: The compound tortoiseshell puts the animal and its shell in one word.
normal.cn: 复合词 tortoiseshell 把动物和壳放进同一个词里。

normal.en: Giant tortoise is used for the huge species of the Galapagos.
normal.cn: giant tortoise 指加拉帕戈斯那种巨型陆龟。

normal.en: Keep tortoise for land animals and turtle for those living in water.
normal.cn: 陆生动物用 tortoise，水生种类用 turtle。

normal.en: The fable of the tortoise and the hare makes slowness a virtue.
normal.cn: 龟兔赛跑的寓言让缓慢成了优点。

normal.en: Compare torturous and tortuous, which look close but come from different roots.
normal.cn: 对比 torturous 与 tortuous，二者形似而词源不同。

abstract.en: See a heavy dome creeping one inch at a time over hot sand.
abstract.cn: 想象一个沉重的穹顶在滚烫的沙地上一次挪动一寸。

abstract.en: Imagine a driver stuck behind a row of slow cars.
abstract.cn: 想象一个司机被一排慢车堵在后面。

abstract.en: Picture a head drawn back into a hard, closed shell.
abstract.cn: 想象一个脑袋缩进又硬又闭的壳里。

examples.en: The tortoise buried itself in the sand before the heat came.
examples.cn: 陆龟在酷热来临前把自己埋进了沙子里。

examples.en: Tourists can still see giant tortoises on the island.
examples.cn: 游客在这个岛上仍能看到巨型陆龟。

examples.en: In the slow lane, he drove like a tortoise all the way home.
examples.cn: 在慢车道上，他像乌龟一样一路开到家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拖铁石」——背着一块铁石在路上拖，一步一挪，正好就是陆龟的样子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 tortuca（陆龟，更早来源不确定）→ 古法语 tortue → 英语先作 tortuce，后改拼为 tortoise。古典拉丁语另有 testudo（陆龟），源于 testa（壳）。

sensesIntro.en: Tortoise begins as the shelled land reptile, then names its shell and material, and finally stands for slowness, patience, and a withdrawn defensive habit.
sensesIntro.cn: tortoise 先指背壳的陆生动物，再指它的壳与龟甲材料，最后用来象征缓慢、坚持与缩壳式自保。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a domed shell creeping over hot sand.
core.cn: 核心意象：穹顶状的硬壳在滚烫沙地上缓缓前行。

branches.en: The shelled land animal is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 背壳的陆生动物是主要义项。

branches.en: A slow mover is the figurative human sense.
branches.cn: 行动迟缓的人是比喻用法。

branches.en: The shell and its worked material are the object sense.
branches.cn: 龟壳及其加材料是实物义项。

branches.en: Patience and defensive withdrawal both grow from the shell.
branches.cn: 耐心与自保退缩都从龟壳这一形象长出。

branches.en: The creature and the slow driver share the same creeping pace.
branches.cn: 这只动物与慢司机共享同样爬行的速度。

intro.en: Tortoise is a borrowing with an uncertain stem, and English builds tortoiseshell from it, while similar-looking tortuous words belong to another family.
intro.cn: tortoise 是词干来源不确定的借词，英语用它构成 tortoiseshell，而形状相近的 tortuous 一类词属于另一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Classical Latin names the animal testudo, from testa, a shell, while tortuca is a later, uncertain form.
latinIntro.cn: 古典拉丁语称这种动物为 testudo（源于 testa，壳），而 tortuca 是较晚且来源不确定的形式。

items.example: Testudo is the classical word for the animal.
items.exampleCN: testudo 是这种动物的古典拉丁语词。

items.example: Testa gives the shell idea.
items.exampleCN: testa 提供「壳」的含义。

items.example: Tortuca is the uncertain medieval form.
items.exampleCN: tortuca 是来源不确定的中世纪形式。

items.example: French tortue carries the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语 tortue 把这个词带入英语。

items.example: English reshapes the French form.
items.exampleCN: 英语改写了法语形式。

items.example: Shell joins tortoise in a compound.
items.exampleCN: shell 与 tortoise 组合成复合词。

items.example: Tortoiseshell names both animal and material.
items.exampleCN: tortoiseshell 既可指龟也指材料。

items.example: The ending -s forms tortoises.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 tortoises。

items.example: Tortuous looks like tortoise but is unrelated.
items.exampleCN: tortuous 看似与 tortoise 相近，实则无关。

definition_zh: 城镇景观；城镇风光；城市景观设计
definition_en: the visual appearance of a town as a whole, or the art of arranging its buildings and open spaces
core_image: 从高处眺望的小镇：屋顶、街道与教堂尖顶连成一幅完整的画
scene: 游客站在山丘上远望，觉得整座小镇像一幅画。From the hilltop, the visitors admired the townscape that stretched to the river.
sceneCN: 这里 townscape 是「城镇景观」（第1个义项：一座城镇整体的视觉外观）；句意：从山丘顶上望去，游客们欣赏着一直延伸到河边的城镇景观。

derivatives.zh: 由 townscape 加 -ing 构成，指城镇景观的营造与规划
由 townscape 与 architect 组合构成，指专做城镇景观的建筑师
与 townscape 同用 -scape 词尾的同类词，指自然或乡村风景

senses.title: The visual character of a town
senses.titleCN: 城镇景观：一座镇的视觉外观
senses.definition: the overall visual appearance of a town, formed by its buildings, streets, and open spaces
senses.definitionCN: 一座城镇由建筑、街道与空地共同形成的整体外观
senses.example: The old townscape is dominated by slate roofs and stone walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城的景观以板岩屋顶和石墙为主。
senses.why: Townscape is town plus the painterly suffix -scape, so it treats a town as a picture one can look at.
senses.whyCN: townscape 由 town 加上绘画性的词尾 -scape 组成，因此它把城镇当成一幅可以观看的画。

senses.title: A picture or photograph of a town
senses.definition: a painting, drawing, or photograph that shows a town view
senses.definitionCN: 展示城镇景色的绘画、素描或照片
senses.example: The museum displays townscapes by local painters.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出本地画家的城镇风景画。
senses.why: Because -scape once meant a picture or view, the word naturally names depicted town views as well.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -scape 本义就是图画或景色，这个词自然也能指被画下来、被拍摄下来的城镇景色。

senses.title: The art of shaping town views
senses.definition: the planning and design of the visual elements of a town, especially in conservation and planning
senses.definitionCN: 在保护与规划中对城镇视觉要素进行的规划与设计
senses.example: Townscape design guides where new buildings may rise.
senses.exampleCN: 城镇景观设计决定新建筑可以建在哪里。
senses.why: Planners turned the descriptive viewing word into a professional field of arranging views.
senses.whyCN: 规划者把这个描述性的「看」的词，变成了专业领域里安排景色的「做」。

senses.title: Built environment of a settlement
senses.definition: the visible built environment of a place people live in, as opposed to the open countryside
senses.definitionCN: 居住地可见的人造环境，与开阔的乡野相对
senses.example: The townscape of the valley has changed little in a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷的城镇风貌一个世纪以来变化很小。
senses.why: The word often stands for the man-made half of a landscape, the part that people have built and rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常代表景观中人造的那一半，即人们建造并不断改造的部分。

senses.title: Urban character in literary description
senses.definition: the mood or atmosphere that a town setting gives to a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 城镇环境赋予一篇作品的氛围或情调
senses.example: His poems borrow the grey townscape of northern cities.
senses.exampleCN: 他的诗借用了北方城市灰色的城市氛围。
senses.why: Writers borrow the viewing image to convey atmosphere, so townscape can mean a mood rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 作家借用「观看」的意象来传达氛围，于是 townscape 可以指一种情调而不是一个地方。

intro.en: Townscape combines the Old English noun town with the suffix -scape, which entered English as a word for a landscape painting.
intro.cn: townscape 由古英语名词 town 与词尾 -scape 组合而成；-scape 最初是作为「风景画」进入英语的。

items.en: Tun means an enclosed place or a village settlement.
items.cn: tun 意为围起来的地方或村庄聚落。

items.en: Landschap names a painted landscape, and English borrows it as landskip.
items.cn: 荷兰语 landschap 指画中的风景，英语借入时写作 landskip。

items.en: The suffix -scape is freed from landscape and forms seascape and then townscape.
items.cn: 词尾 -scape 从 landscape 中独立出来，先构成 seascape，再构成 townscape。

items.en: Townscape is used by artists and early planners for the view of a town.
items.cn: 艺术家与早期规划者用 townscape 指一座城镇的景色。

items.en: Townscape becomes a technical term in urban conservation and design.
items.cn: townscape 成为城市保护与设计中的专业术语。

note.en: Townscape belongs to the -scape word family and sits close to general scenery words.
note.cn: townscape 属于 -scape 词族，并与表示「景色」的一般词相邻。

entries.definition: the visible features of an area of land
entries.definitionCN: 陆地某区域的可见特征（与 townscape 同用 -scape 词尾）

entries.definition: a view or picture of the sea
entries.definitionCN: 海景；海景画（与 townscape 同用 -scape 词尾）

entries.definition: the appearance of a large city
entries.definitionCN: 城市景观（与 townscape 结构相同，但指更大的城市）

entries.definition: the general appearance of natural surroundings
entries.definitionCN: 景色；风景，多指自然环境

entries.definition: the conditions and objects around a place
entries.definitionCN: 周围环境；周边景物

entries.definition: the outline of buildings against the sky
entries.definitionCN: 天际线；建筑轮廓（是城镇景观的轮廓部分）

normalIntro.en: Townscape is town seen as a picture, built from a painterly suffix and a planning vocabulary.
normalIntro.cn: townscape 是把城镇当作一幅画来看，由绘画词尾与规划词汇共同构成。

normal.en: Town plus scape, as in landscape and seascape, means the view of a town.
normal.cn: town 加上 landscape 里的 -scape，就得到「城镇的景色」。

normal.en: A townscape is what you see when you look at a town from outside.
normal.cn: townscape 就是你从外面看一座城镇时看到的东西。

normal.en: Planners speak of townscape management when they protect views.
normal.cn: 规划者保护景观时，会说 townscape management。

normal.en: Historic townscape appears in reports on heritage protection.
normal.cn: historic townscape 常出现在遗产保护报告里。

normal.en: Compare cityscape: townscape for small towns, cityscape for big cities.
normal.cn: 对比 cityscape：小镇用 townscape，大城市用 cityscape。

abstract.en: Picture a postcard showing a whole town in one view.
abstract.cn: 想象一张明信片，把整座小镇收进同一个画面。

abstract.en: Imagine a painter standing on a hill with an easel facing the town.
abstract.cn: 想象一位画家站在山丘上，把画架朝向小镇。

abstract.en: Think of a planning map where colored blocks fit together like a picture.
abstract.cn: 想象一张规划图，彩色区块像拼图一样拼成一幅画。

examples.en: The townscape is a mix of medieval lanes and modern shops.
examples.cn: 这里的城镇景观融合了中世纪小巷与现代商店。

examples.en: New towers have changed the townscape beyond recognition.
examples.cn: 新建的高楼让这座城市的面貌变得面目全非。

examples.en: A townscape painter captured the market square at dusk.
examples.cn: 一位城镇风景画家画下了黄昏时的集市广场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「淘客 + 素描」——游客一边逛街一边素描，画出的就是城镇景观；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 town（围起的村落）+ 英语词尾 -scape（源自荷兰语 landschap「风景画」）→ townscape，核心义「把城镇当作一幅画来看」。

sensesIntro.en: Townscape starts as the visual character of a town, widens to pictures and to the planning discipline, then covers the built environment and literary atmosphere.
sensesIntro.cn: townscape 从「城镇的视觉外观」出发，扩展到城景画与景观规划，再延伸到建成风貌与文学氛围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole town gathered into one framed view.
core.cn: 核心意象：整座城镇被收进一幅有边框的画面。

branches.en: The overall look of a town is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 城镇的整体外观是日常义项。

branches.en: Paintings and photographs turn the view into an image.
branches.cn: 绘画与照片把这个「看」变成了一件影像作品。

branches.en: Planning turns the view into a discipline.
branches.cn: 规划把这种景观变成一门专业。

branches.en: Both name the built side of a landscape.
branches.cn: 两者都指景观中由人建造的那一面。

branches.en: The pictorial view carries mood into literature.
branches.cn: 图画式的看法把情调带进了文学。

intro.en: Townscape is a compound built on town, with the productive suffix -scape behind a large family of view words.
intro.cn: townscape 是以 town 为基础的复合词，其后的 -scape 是一个能产的词尾，构出了一大批表示「景」的词。

latinIntro.en: Neither town nor -scape is Latin: town is Old English and -scape comes through Dutch from a Germanic root for shaping.
latinIntro.cn: town 与 -scape 都不是拉丁语：town 来自古英语，-scape 经荷兰语来自日耳曼语表示「塑造」的词根。

items.example: Town gives the word its built subject.
items.exampleCN: town 提供了这个词的人造主体。

items.meaning: a view or picture of an area
items.meaningCN: 某片区域的景色或图画
items.example: The suffix -scape marks a framed view.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -scape 表示被框住的景色。

items.example: Landscape is the model for all -scape words.
items.exampleCN: landscape 是所有 -scape 词的范本。

items.example: Seascape shows the suffix working alone.
items.exampleCN: seascape 说明这个词尾能独立构词。

items.example: Cityscape is the large-town partner of townscape.
items.exampleCN: cityscape 是 townscape 对应大城市的版本。

items.example: Townspeople shares the base word town.
items.exampleCN: townspeople 共享基础词 town。

items.example: -ship marks a place or condition.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ship 常表示地点或状态。

items.meaning: the visual character of a town
items.example: Townscape joins a place to a view.
items.exampleCN: townscape 把地点与景色连在一起。

items.example: The -ing form names the activity.
items.exampleCN: -ing 形式表示这种活动本身。

definition_zh: 毒素；毒质
definition_en: a poisonous substance produced by a living organism, especially by bacteria, plants, or animals
core_image: 一只小生物悄悄放出一滴看不见的毒液，侵入另一具身体
scene: 科学家发现，某种细菌会放出一种让人发烧的物质。The scientists found that the bacteria release a toxin that causes fever.
sceneCN: 这里 toxin 是「毒素」（第1个义项：生物体产生的有毒物质）；句意：科学家发现这种细菌会释放一种引起发烧的毒素。

derivatives.zh: 由 toxin 加 -genic（产生）构成，指能产生毒素的
由 toxic 加 -ity 构成，指毒性；毒力
由 toxico- 加 -logy 构成，指毒理学
由 de- 与 tox- 构成，指解毒；去毒

senses.title: Poison made by a living organism
senses.definition: a poisonous substance that is produced by a living organism, such as a bacterium, plant, or animal
senses.definitionCN: 由细菌、植物或动物等活生物产生的有毒物质
senses.example: The bacterium secretes a toxin that attacks nerve cells.
senses.exampleCN: 这种细菌分泌一种攻击神经细胞的毒素。
senses.why: Toxin was coined from the Greek word for a bow, whose arrow carried poison, so the word names a poison made by a living thing.
senses.whyCN: toxin 由希腊语「弓」一词造出，弓上的箭涂着毒，所以这个词专指活生物制造出来的毒。

senses.title: A biological poison distinguished from chemical poisons
senses.definition: a biological poison, kept distinct from man-made or mineral poisons in scientific usage
senses.definitionCN: 科学用法中有别于人造毒物或矿物毒物的生物性毒物
senses.example: Lead is a poison, but it is not a toxin.
senses.exampleCN: 铅是有毒的，但它不是毒素。
senses.why: Precise science needs the difference, so toxin is narrowed to substances that organisms themselves make.
senses.whyCN: 严谨的科学需要区分，于是 toxin 被限定为生物自己制造的物质。

senses.title: Harmful substance in everyday talk
senses.definition: a harmful substance in general, as the word is loosely used in health and lifestyle writing
senses.definitionCN: 泛指有害物质，常见于健康与生活方式类文章的宽松用法
senses.example: The diet promises to flush out toxins from the body.
senses.exampleCN: 这种饮食法声称能排出体内毒素。
senses.why: Popular writing stretched the scientific term until it means any unwanted harmful substance.
senses.whyCN: 通俗文章把这个科学术语拉伸了，使它变成指任何不应有的有害物质。

senses.title: The harmful element in a phrase
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：某项事物中的「毒」
senses.definition: a harmful or corrupting element seen as poisoning places or situations
senses.definitionCN: 被视为污染某地或某种局面的有害、腐蚀性因素
senses.example: Critics call advertising a toxin in the public sphere.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把广告称为公共领域中的毒素。
senses.why: The medical image of poison spreads to social life, where bad influences are said to poison a place.
senses.whyCN: 「毒」的医学意象延伸到社会生活，坏影响被说成毒害一个地方，于是 toxin 成了这种有害因素的代称。

intro.en: Toxin is a scientific coinage from 1886, built from the Greek word toxikon, the poison used on arrows, by way of Latin toxicum and the combining form toxico-.
intro.cn: toxin 是 1886 年出现的科学新造词，由希腊语 toxikon（涂在箭上的毒）经拉丁语 toxicum 和组合形式 toxico- 构成。

items.en: Toxon means a bow, and toxikon pharmakon is arrow poison.
items.cn: toxon 意为「弓」，toxikon pharmakon 指「箭毒」。

items.en: Toxicum names any poison, dropping the word for bow.
items.cn: 拉丁语 toxicum 泛指毒物，丢掉了「弓」的部分。

items.en: Toxic and the combining form toxico- enter medical English.
items.cn: toxic 与组合形式 toxico- 进入英语医学词汇。

items.en: Toxin is coined for organic poisons produced by bacteria.
items.cn: toxin 被造出，专指细菌产生的有机毒素。

items.en: Toxin gives rise to toxicology, antitoxin, and everyday talk of body toxins.
items.cn: toxin 衍生出 toxicology、antitoxin，以及口语中「体内毒素」的说法。

note.en: Toxin shares the Greek arrow-poison root tox- with a family of medical words and stands near everyday words for poison.
note.cn: toxin 与一批医学词共享希腊语「箭毒」词根 tox-，并与日常表示「毒」的词相邻。

entries.definition: poisonous
entries.definitionCN: 有毒的（与 toxin 同用 tox- 词根）

entries.definition: an antibody that neutralizes a toxin
entries.definitionCN: 中和毒素的抗体；抗毒素（由 anti- 加 toxin 构成）

entries.definition: the study of poisons
entries.definitionCN: 毒理学（toxico- 与 -logy 组成，与 toxin 同源）

entries.definition: a substance that harms or kills living things
entries.definitionCN: 能伤害或杀死生物的物质（可包括矿物与人造物）

entries.definition: poison injected by a snake, insect, or spider
entries.definitionCN: 蛇、昆虫或蜘蛛注入的毒液

entries.definition: a weakened toxin used in vaccines
entries.definitionCN: 用于疫苗的减毒毒素；类毒素

normalIntro.en: Toxin carries an arrow in its name: the poison the ancient Greeks put on arrowheads.
normalIntro.cn: toxin 的名字里藏着一支箭：古希腊人涂在箭头上的毒。

normal.en: The tox- root in toxin comes from Greek toxon, a bow.
normal.cn: toxin 中 tox- 词根来自希腊语 toxon，意为「弓」。

normal.en: Toxin and toxic share the same root, so a toxin makes you sick.
normal.cn: toxin 与 toxic 同根，所以毒素会让人中毒。

normal.en: An antitoxin acts against a toxin.
normal.cn: antitoxin（抗毒素）就是对抗 toxin 的物质。

normal.en: Bacterial toxin is the most common phrase in medical texts.
normal.cn: bacterial toxin 是医学文本中最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Compare poison and venom: a toxin is made by a living organism.
normal.cn: 对比 poison 与 venom：toxin 特指活生物制造出来的。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny bow shooting an invisible poison into the blood.
abstract.cn: 想象一把很小的弓，把看不见的毒射进血液。

abstract.en: Imagine a gas mask sealed on as a warning sign lights up.
abstract.cn: 想象防毒面具扣紧，警示灯亮起。

abstract.en: Think of a sink slowly filling with dirty water nobody drains.
abstract.cn: 想象水槽里慢慢积满脏水，却没人去疏通。

examples.en: Doctors tested the patient for bacterial toxins.
examples.cn: 医生为病人检验了细菌毒素。

examples.en: Some plants protect themselves with powerful toxins.
examples.cn: 有些植物用强力毒素保护自己。

examples.en: Antibodies can neutralise a toxin before it reaches the brain.
examples.cn: 抗体能在毒素到达脑部之前将它中和。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托克辛」——把「毒」托去侵蚀别人，于是成了毒素；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 toxon（弓）→ toxikon pharmakon（箭毒）→ 拉丁语 toxicum（毒物）→ 英语 toxico- / toxic → toxin（生物产生的毒素），核心义「箭上涂的毒」。

sensesIntro.en: Toxin begins as a poison made by a living organism, is narrowed against chemical poisons, then loosens in everyday and figurative speech.
sensesIntro.cn: toxin 先指活生物制造的毒，再在与化学毒物的对比中被限定，最后在口语与比喻中放宽为各种「有害的东西」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of arrow poison hidden in a living body.
core.cn: 核心意象：藏在活物体内的一滴箭毒。

branches.en: A poison produced by an organism is the scientific core.
branches.cn: 生物产生的毒是这个词的科学核心义。

branches.en: The contrast with chemical poisons narrows the term.
branches.cn: 与化学毒物的对比使这个术语更窄。

branches.en: Loose health writing widens it to any harmful substance.
branches.cn: 浅俗的健康文章把它扩大到任何有害物质。

branches.en: A physical poison and a poisoning influence share one image.
branches.cn: 实在的毒物与毒害性的影响共享同一个意象。

branches.en: The precise and the loose uses pull the word in two directions.
branches.cn: 严谨用法与宽松用法把这个词拉向两个方向。

intro.en: Toxin is a modern scientific compound of Greek roots, with the tox- element at the heart of a large medical family.
intro.cn: toxin 是由希腊语词根构成的近代科学词，其核心部分 tox- 位于一大批医学词的中心。

latinIntro.en: The Greek toxikon passed into Latin as toxicum, the general word for poison.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 toxikon 进入拉丁语后成为 toxicum，泛指毒物。

items.example: The root tox- carries the bow image.
items.exampleCN: 词根 tox- 承载着「弓」的意象。

items.example: The suffix -in marks a named substance.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -in 表示一种具体物质。

items.example: Toxic is the adjective partner of toxin.
items.exampleCN: toxic 是 toxin 的形容词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ity names a quality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 表示某种性质。

items.example: The suffix -logy names a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -logy 表示学科领域。

items.meaning: a substance that works against a toxin
items.example: The prefix anti- means against.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 anti- 表示「对抗」。

items.example: The prefix de- reverses the action.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 表示去除、逆转。

items.example: The suffix -oid means like or resembling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oid 表示「类似」。

items.example: The suffix -emia refers to blood conditions.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -emia 表示血液方面的病症。

latinEntries.example: Toxicum is the Latin bridge into modern terms.
latinEntries.exampleCN: toxicum 是通向现代术语的拉丁语桥梁。

definition_zh: 气管炎
definition_en: inflammation of the trachea, the windpipe that carries air from the throat to the lungs
core_image: 喉咙下方那根送气的管子，内壁发红、肿胀、发炎了
scene: 孩子咳嗽不止，喉咙里发出粗重的呼吸声。The child kept coughing, and the doctor diagnosed tracheitis.
sceneCN: 这里 tracheitis 是「气管炎」（第1个义项：气管发炎）；句意：这个孩子一直咳嗽，医生诊断为气管炎。

derivatives.zh: 由 trachea 加 -al 构成，指气管的
由 tracheo- 与 -tomy（切开）构成，指气管切开术
由 laryngo-（喉）与 tracheitis 复合构成，指喉气管炎

senses.title: Inflammation of the windpipe
senses.definition: an inflammation of the trachea, often caused by infection and marked by coughing and hoarseness
senses.definitionCN: 气管的炎症，多由感染引起，表现为咳嗽和声音嘶哑
senses.example: Tracheitis often follows a severe cold.
senses.exampleCN: 气管炎常常在重感冒之后出现。
senses.why: The word joins the Greek name for the windpipe with the medical suffix meaning inflammation, so it names the inflamed tube itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊语对气管的称呼与表示「发炎」的医学词尾连在一起，因此它指的是发炎的那根管子本身。

senses.title: A cough and hoarseness centred on the windpipe
senses.titleCN: 以气管为中心的咳嗽与嘶哑
senses.definition: the symptoms of a chesty cough and hoarse voice that doctors group under this label
senses.definitionCN: 医生归在这一名称下的带痰咳嗽与声音嘶哑等症状
senses.example: His tracheitis left him hoarse for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他的气管炎让他嘶哑了一个星期。
senses.why: Patients name a condition by its complaint, so the inflammation label comes to stand for the cough it causes.
senses.whyCN: 病人用症状给病命名，于是「发炎」这个病理标签也用来表示它引起的咳嗽。

senses.title: Acute bacterial windpipe infection
senses.definition: a severe acute bacterial infection of the trachea, mainly seen in young children
senses.definitionCN: 一种主要见于幼儿的严重急性细菌性气管感染
senses.example: Bacterial tracheitis can cause a dangerous high fever in children.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌性气管炎可能使儿童出现危险的高烧。
senses.why: Clinical use tightens the general term to one serious infectious form that needs urgent care.
senses.whyCN: 临床用法把这个一般性术语收窄为一种需要紧急处理的严重感染类型。

senses.title: Loose mention of any throat infection
senses.definition: an informal use covering any infection of the throat and upper airways
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中泛指咽喉与上呼吸道的感染
senses.example: In local usage, many sore throats are simply called tracheitis.
senses.exampleCN: 在当地的日常说法里，许多嗓子疼都被简单叫作气管炎。
senses.why: Outside hospitals the label spreads from the tube to nearby throat complaints that ordinary speakers cannot tell apart.
senses.whyCN: 在医院之外，这个标签从气管蔓延到附近的咽喉不适，因为普通人分不清这些部位。
