intro.en: Tracheitis is a coinage from Greek: tracheia arteria means the rough artery, the windpipe, and the suffix -itis marks inflammation.
intro.cn: tracheitis 是希腊语来源的医学新造词：tracheia arteria 意为「粗糙的动脉」，即气管，词尾 -itis 表示炎症。

items.en: Tracheia arteria means the rough artery, named for its ridged rings.
items.cn: tracheia arteria 意为「粗糙的动脉」，因其软骨环的凹凸而得名。

items.en: Anatomists shorten the phrase to trachea.
items.cn: 解剖学家把这个词组简化为 trachea。

items.en: The ending -itis already meant inflammation in Greek medicine.
items.cn: 词尾 -itis 在希腊医学中就已表示炎症。

items.en: Tracheitis is formed by attaching -itis to the new anatomical name.
items.cn: tracheitis 是在新的解剖学名称后接 -itis 构成的。

items.en: Tracheitis enters clinical English as the standard diagnosis for windpipe inflammation.
items.cn: tracheitis 进入临床英语，成为气管炎症的标准病名。

note.en: Tracheitis is a medically built noun: the trachea plus the inflammation suffix, beside a large family of -itis diseases.
note.cn: tracheitis 是医学构词：trachea（气管）加上炎症词尾，旁边是一大批以 -itis 结尾的病名。

entries.definition: the windpipe
entries.definitionCN: 气管（tracheitis 的基础词）

entries.definition: a surgical cut into the windpipe
entries.definitionCN: 气管切开术（与 tracheitis 同用 trache- 词根）

entries.definition: inflammation of the airways in the lungs
entries.definitionCN: 支气管炎（与 tracheitis 同用 -itis 炎症词尾）

entries.definition: inflammation of the voice box
entries.definitionCN: 喉炎（炎症部位紧邻气管上方）

entries.definition: a childhood illness with a barking cough
entries.definitionCN: 哮吼（一种儿童咳嗽音粗的呼吸道疾病）

entries.definition: a rough, hard voice
entries.definitionCN: 声音嘶哑（气管炎的常见症状）

normalIntro.en: Tracheitis is the windpipe plus the inflammation suffix: the Greek tube name and the near-universal -itis.
normalIntro.cn: tracheitis 就是「气管」加上「发炎」词尾：希腊语的管名和几乎通用的 -itis。

normal.en: Trache- names the windpipe, as in trachea and tracheotomy.
normal.cn: trache- 表示气管，见 trachea 与 tracheotomy。

normal.en: The suffix -itis means inflammation in bronchitis and laryngitis.
normal.cn: 词尾 -itis 表示发炎，如 bronchitis 与 laryngitis。

normal.en: Trachea plus -itis gives tracheitis, an inflamed windpipe.
normal.cn: trachea 加 -itis 得到 tracheitis，即发炎的气管。

normal.en: Acute tracheitis is a common phrase in medical writing.
normal.cn: acute tracheitis（急性气管炎）是医学写作中的常见说法。

normal.en: Compare bronchitis: same suffix, but the inflammation is lower down.
normal.cn: 对比 bronchitis：词尾相同，但发炎的位置更低。

abstract.en: Picture a tube with red, swollen rings glowing along its walls.
abstract.cn: 想象一根管子，内壁的圆环一圈圈发红肿胀。

abstract.en: Imagine a cough shaking a whole small chest at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一阵咳嗽震动着小小的胸膛。

abstract.en: Think of a warning sticker on a pipe that marks out the inflamed section.
abstract.cn: 想象在管子上贴一张警示贴纸，标出那段发炎的部位。

examples.en: The doctor confirmed that her tracheitis was bacterial.
examples.cn: 医生确认她的气管炎是细菌性的。

examples.en: Tracheitis in children requires close attention to breathing.
examples.cn: 儿童的气管炎需要密切留意呼吸情况。

examples.en: Smoking makes chronic tracheitis much harder to treat.
examples.cn: 吸烟会让慢性气管炎更难以治疗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹气 + 炎」——吹气要经过的那根管子发了炎，就是气管炎；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 tracheia arteria（粗糙的动脉，即气管）→ 拉丁语解剖学 trachea（气管）+ 希腊语词尾 -itis（炎症）→ tracheitis（气管炎），核心义「气管发炎」。

sensesIntro.en: Tracheitis begins as the inflammation of the windpipe, is felt through its cough and hoarseness, narrows to a severe bacterial infection, and loosens into a general word for throat infection.
sensesIntro.cn: tracheitis 先指气管的炎症，再经由咳嗽与嘶哑的症状被感知，又在临床上收窄为一种严重的细菌感染，最后在口语中放宽为泛指咽喉感染。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ridged air tube swollen and red inside the throat.
core.cn: 核心意象：喉咙里那根带环的送气管内壁红肿。

branches.en: Inflammation of the trachea is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 气管发炎是这个词的字面义。

branches.en: The cough and hoarse voice are the symptoms people name.
branches.cn: 咳嗽与声音嘶哑是人们用来称呼它的症状。

branches.en: The severe bacterial form is the clinical narrowing.
branches.cn: 严重的细菌型是临床用法上的收窄。

branches.en: The inflamed tube shows itself through the cough.
branches.cn: 发炎的气管正是通过咳嗽显现出来。

branches.en: Everyday speech stretches the symptom word to any throat infection.
branches.cn: 日常说法把症状词扩展到任何咽喉感染。

intro.en: Tracheitis is a medical compound: the Greek tube name trache- plus the inflammation suffix -itis.
intro.cn: tracheitis 是医学复合词：希腊语表示管子的词根 trache- 加上表示炎症的词尾 -itis。

latinIntro.en: Both parts come from Greek: tracheia arteria for the windpipe and -itis for inflammation, recorded together in medical Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都来自希腊语：tracheia arteria 指气管，-itis 指炎症，二者在医学拉丁语中合用。

items.meaning: rough, and by extension the windpipe
items.example: The root trache- names the ridged tube.
items.exampleCN: 词根 trache- 指那根带环的管子。

items.example: The suffix -itis marks inflammation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -itis 表示发炎。

items.example: Trachea is the full noun behind tracheitis.
items.exampleCN: trachea 是 tracheitis 背后的完整名词。

items.example: The suffix -al forms a relating adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成表示「与……有关」的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -tomy marks a surgical cut.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tomy 表示外科切开。

items.example: Tracheotomy shows the same root in surgery.
items.exampleCN: tracheotomy 显示同一词根用在外科术语里。

items.example: Bronchitis repeats the -itis pattern.
items.exampleCN: bronchitis 沿用了 -itis 的模式。

items.meaning: inflammation of the voice box and windpipe
items.example: Laryngotracheitis stacks two sites on one word.
items.exampleCN: laryngotracheitis 把两个部位叠在一个词上。

items.example: The suffix -ectomy marks removal in surgery.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ectomy 表示外科切除。

latinEntries.example: Trachea is the anatomical name used in Latin texts.
latinEntries.exampleCN: trachea 是拉丁文解剖学著作中的名称。

latinEntries.example: Arteria aspera is the older Latin name for the windpipe.
latinEntries.exampleCN: arteria aspera 是气管较早的拉丁名。

definition_zh: 大片土地；区域；带；束；道；小册子
definition_en: a large area of land; also a connected system of organs or nerve fibres, or a short political or religious pamphlet
core_image: 被拉长拉直的一片地：一条不断向远处延伸的带子
scene: 土地管理局的公告栏上贴着一份新发布的小册子，介绍西部的一大片荒原。A new tract on the office board describes the empty land in the west.
sceneCN: 这里 tract 是「小册子」（第 4 个义项：短小的政治或宗教册子）；句意：办公室公告栏上一份新的小册子介绍了西部的荒原。

derivatives.zh: 基础词加名词后缀构成，义为「牵引力；牵引治疗」
基础词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「拖拉机」
由拉丁语 tractare 加分词后缀构成，义为「易驾驭的；温顺的」
前缀 ex-（向外）加 trahere，义为「拔出；提取；提取物」
前缀 abs-（离开）加 trahere，义为「抽象的；从具体中抽离的」

senses.title: A large stretch of land
senses.definition: a large area of land, especially one that is empty or used for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 一大片土地，尤指空旷或用于特定用途的区域
senses.example: They bought a tract of land beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边买下了一大片土地。
senses.why: Latin tractus means a drawing out or stretch, and land drawn out into one long stretch becomes a tract of land.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tractus 意为「拉出、延伸」，把土地拉长伸展成一片，就成了大片土地。

senses.title: A connected passage inside the body
senses.definition: a system of connected organs or a band of nerve fibres that carry something along
senses.definitionCN: 身体内相互连接的器官系统或输送物质的神经纤维束
senses.example: The doctor examined his respiratory tract.
senses.exampleCN: 医生检查了他的呼吸道。
senses.why: A tract is a line drawn from one point to another, so an internal passage that carries air, food, or nerve signals along a line is also a tract.
senses.whyCN: tract 是两点之间拉出的一条线，所以体内沿着一条线运送空气、食物或神经信号的通路也叫 tract。

senses.title: A group of similar things drawn out together
senses.definition: a large extent of something that can be sensed, such as sound, light, or clouds
senses.definitionCN: 可被感知的一大片连续之物，如声音、光或云
senses.example: Tracts of grey cloud moved across the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 成片灰色的云从山谷上空移过。
senses.why: The idea of stretching out applies to anything continuous, so a wide stretch of cloud or sound is described as tracts.
senses.whyCN: 「拉伸铺开」的想法可用于任何连续之物，因此大片的云或声音都可以用 tract 来描述。

senses.title: A short printed pamphlet
senses.definition: a short piece of writing, often political or religious, printed and given out to people
senses.definitionCN: 篇幅短小的文章，多为政治或宗教内容，印成小册子发给人们
senses.example: The group handed out a political tract at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团体在车站发放政治小册子。
senses.why: A tract is something drawn out as a single piece, and early printed sheets drawn out into one short essay gave the word a publishing sense.
senses.whyCN: tract 指拉成一整块的东西，早期印成一张张的小文章被拉成一篇短文，于是这个词就有了小册子的含义。

senses.title: A long period of time
senses.definition: a long and continuing period of time, used mainly in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 一段漫长而持续的时间，多用于正式书面语
senses.example: The whole region lay silent for a long tract of years.
senses.exampleCN: 整个地区在一段漫长的岁月里保持沉寂。
senses.why: If a stretch of land can be long, a stretch of time can be long too, so a drawn out period of years is called a tract of time.
senses.whyCN: 土地可以拉得很长，时间也可以拉得很长，所以一段漫长的年月就说成 tract of time。

intro.en: Tract comes from Latin tractus, a drawing or stretch, the past participle of trahere, to draw or pull.
intro.cn: tract 来自拉丁语 tractus（拉、延伸），是动词 trahere（拉、拽）的过去分词。

items.en: Trahere means to draw, pull, or drag along.
items.cn: trahere 意为拉、拽或拖动。

items.en: Tractus names a drawing out, a course, or a stretch of space.
items.cn: tractus 指拉出、行程或一段空间。

items.en: Tractatus is used for a written treatment of a subject.
items.cn: 中古拉丁语用 tractatus 指对某一课题的论述。

items.en: The English word first names a written work on a subject.
items.cn: 英语中此词最初指论及某主题的书面作品。

items.en: The land sense of a long stretch of country develops.
items.cn: 指一大片土地的义项在此时发展出来。

items.en: Science uses tract for passages in the body, as in the gut.
items.cn: 现代科学用 tract 指体内的通路，如肠道。

note.en: Tract belongs to the Latin trahere family, whose forms appear in many everyday words that mean pulling.
note.cn: tract 属于拉丁语 trahere 词族，这个词族的成员出现在许多表示「拉」的常用词里。

entries.definition: the ability to grip a surface, or the pulling of a part
entries.definitionCN: 抓地力；牵引

entries.definition: a vehicle used for pulling farm equipment
entries.definitionCN: 拖拉机

entries.definition: to pull someone or something towards you
entries.definitionCN: 吸引（字面义为「拉向」）

entries.definition: a path or marks left by movement
entries.definitionCN: 小径；足迹（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自古法语 trac）

entries.definition: a part of a place or a measured space
entries.definitionCN: 地区；面积（中性而通用）

entries.definition: a continuous extent of land or water
entries.definitionCN: 一片（土地或水域）

entries.definition: a very short printed book
entries.definitionCN: 小册子（无宗教政治色彩）

normalIntro.en: Tract is the stretched out line: land drawn into a strip, a passage drawn through the body, a single sheet drawn into a booklet.
normalIntro.cn: tract 是「被拉长拉直的一条」：土地拉成一条带，身体拉出一条道，一张纸拉成一本小册。

normal.en: A tract of land is a long stretch of country.
normal.cn: a tract of land 就是一片纵长的乡野之地。

normal.en: The digestive tract moves food along like a pipe.
normal.cn: 消化道像管道一样把食物向前运送。

normal.en: The optic tract carries signals from the eye to the brain.
normal.cn: 视束把信号从眼睛传到大脑。

normal.en: The same root gives tractor, attraction, and extract.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 tractor、attraction 与 extract。

normal.en: Compare track: track is a path or footprint, tract is a stretch or passage.
normal.cn: 对比 track：track 是小径或足迹，tract 是延伸的一片或一条通路。

abstract.en: Picture a ribbon untied on a table, lying long and flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一条在桌上摊开的长丝带，又长又平。

abstract.en: See a corridor running from a door to another door.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，从一扇门一直通到另一扇门。

abstract.en: Imagine a wide band of cloud pushed across the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一条宽宽的云带被推过天空。

examples.en: Vast tracts of forest were cleared for farming.
examples.cn: 大片森林被砍伐开垦为农田。

examples.en: Damage to the intestinal tract can be serious.
examples.cn: 肠道的损伤可能很严重。

examples.en: He wrote a short tract attacking the new tax on tea.
examples.cn: 他写了一份短小的小册子抨击新的茶叶税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「戳克特」——用尺子一戳，拉出一条长「带」，就是一片地、一条道；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trahere（拉、拽，过去分词 tractus）→ 名词 tractus（拉出；延伸；一段）→ 中世纪拉丁语 tractatus（论述）→ 英语 tract，核心义「被拉长拉直的一片或一条」。

sensesIntro.en: Tract starts from a stretch of land, then stretches into passages inside the body and wide bands in the sky, and finally names a short printed piece.
sensesIntro.cn: tract 先指一片被拉展开的土地，再延伸为体内的道与成片的天空之物，最后指印成短文的小册子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long strip drawn out and held taut.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被拉长拉直的带子。

branches.en: A stretch of land is the plainest sense of something drawn out wide.
branches.cn: 一片土地是最直接的「拉展开」的义项。

branches.en: A passage inside the body is the medical sense.
branches.cn: 体内的道是医学义项。

branches.en: A wide band of cloud or sound is the poetic extension.
branches.cn: 成片的云或声音是诗意的延伸。

branches.en: A short printed piece carries the idea of a single drawn sheet.
branches.cn: 短小的印刷品沿用了「拉成一片纸」的想法。

branches.en: Both land and time can be stretched out, so a tract can cover either.
branches.cn: 土地与时间都能被拉长，所以 tract 既能指地也能指时间。

intro.en: The root tract comes from Latin trahere, to pull, and builds a large family from extract to traction.
intro.cn: 词根 tract 源自拉丁语 trahere（拉），并构成从 extract 到 traction 的庞大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere and its participle tractus mean pulled, drawn out, or a stretch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 及其分词 tractus 意为拉、拉出，或指一段延伸。

items.example: Trahere is the parent verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: trahere 是整个词族的母动词。

items.example: Tractus gives English its name for a strip of land.
items.exampleCN: tractus 给英语提供了指一片土地的词。

items.meaning: action or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或动作结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion turns tract into traction.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 把 tract 变成 traction。

items.example: Traction names the power of pulling.
items.exampleCN: traction 表示牵引的力量。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 表示做事的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -or forms tractor.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 tractor。

items.example: A tractor pulls farm machines across a field.
items.exampleCN: 拖拉机拉着农机在田里行驶。

items.example: With extract the prefix means out.
items.exampleCN: 在 extract 里这个前缀表示向外。

items.example: Extract means to pull something out.
items.exampleCN: extract 表示把某物拉出来。

items.example: The prefix abs- forms abstract.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 abs- 构成 abstract。

items.example: Abstract describes ideas removed from physical things.
items.exampleCN: abstract 描述脱离具体事物的观念。

items.example: Contract means to draw together.
items.exampleCN: contract 表示拉拢、收缩。

definition_zh: 悲惨的；悲剧的；令人极为惋惜的
definition_en: causing great sadness, especially because of death or suffering; also relating to serious drama
core_image: 舞台上戴面具的演员：欢乐被命运撕碎，结局无可挽回
scene: 一场暴雨冲走了整个村庄，人们失去家园。News of the tragic flood spread quickly through the town.
sceneCN: 这里 tragic 是「悲惨的」（第 1 个义项：造成巨大悲痛的事件）；句意：这场悲惨洪水的消息迅速传遍了小镇。

derivatives.zh: 基础词对应的名词，义为「悲剧；惨事」
基础词加副词后缀 -ly，义为「悲惨地」
tragic 与 comic 合成，义为「悲喜交加的」
由 tragedy 加表示人物的后缀构成，义为「悲剧演员；悲剧作家」

senses.title: Causing great sadness through death or disaster
senses.definition: extremely sad because it involves death, serious injury, or great suffering
senses.definitionCN: 因涉及死亡、重伤或巨大痛苦而极其令人悲伤的
senses.example: It was a tragic accident on the icy bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这是发生在结冰桥上的一场惨烈事故。
senses.why: Greek drama showed human joy crushed by fate, and the word carried that weight of unavoidable sorrow into everyday reports of disasters.
senses.whyCN: 希腊戏剧展示人的欢乐被命运碾碎，这个词把那层无法避免的悲伤带进了日常的灾难报道。

senses.title: Relating to tragedy as a dramatic form
senses.definition: connected with tragedy as a serious form of drama with an unhappy end
senses.definitionCN: 与以不幸结局收场的严肃戏剧体裁悲剧相关的
senses.example: Shakespeare wrote several tragic plays late in his life.
senses.exampleCN: 莎士比亚在晚年写了多部悲剧。
senses.why: The adjective began in the theatre, describing plays that follow a great person to a ruinous end.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最初用于剧场，描述跟随一位大人物走向毁灭结局的剧本。

senses.title: Sad because a failure cannot be avoided
senses.definition: sad or disappointing because something good is lost through unhappy circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 因不佳的处境使好事落空而感到悲伤或遗憾的
senses.example: It is tragic that the old theatre had to close.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老剧院不得不关门，令人惋惜。
senses.why: If a fall is tragic on the stage, any real loss that feels unavoidable can be called tragic too.
senses.whyCN: 既然舞台上的坠落可以用 tragic 形容，现实中任何看似无可避免的损失也可以用 tragic 形容。

senses.title: The character of a tragic hero
senses.definition: having the dignity and flaw found in the main figure of a tragedy
senses.definitionCN: 具备悲剧主人公那种尊严与缺陷的
senses.example: He had a tragic flaw that led to his own ruin.
senses.exampleCN: 他有一个导致自身毁灭的悲剧性缺陷。
senses.why: Greek tragedy gave its hero a fault that made the fall seem both deserved and unescapable.
senses.whyCN: 希腊悲剧给主人公一个缺陷，使坠落既看似应得又无法逃避。

senses.title: A tragic style in writing or art
senses.definition: using the serious and elevated style of tragedy in writing, music, or art
senses.definitionCN: 在写作、音乐或艺术中采用悲剧那种严肃而崇高的风格的
senses.example: The novel ends on a tragic note of loss.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说以失落这一悲剧性的笔调结尾。
senses.why: Anything written or performed in the elevated manner of tragedy can be described as tragic in style.
senses.whyCN: 凡以悲剧那种崇高方式写作或表演的作品，都可以说在风格上是 tragic。

intro.en: Tragic comes from Greek tragikos, from tragoidia, tragedy, and is linked in one account to tragos, a goat.
intro.cn: tragic 来自希腊语 tragikos，源自 tragoidia（悲剧），一种说法认为其与 tragos（山羊）有关。

items.en: Tragoidia names the serious sung drama of Athens.
items.cn: 希腊语 tragoidia 指雅典的严肃歌唱戏剧。

items.en: A common account links it to tragos, goat, but the origin is debated.
items.cn: 一般认为其与 tragos（山羊）有关，但起源有争议。

items.en: Tragicus enters Latin as the adjective for tragedy.
items.cn: tragoedia 与 tragicus 进入拉丁语，成为「悲剧」及其形容词。

items.en: Tragique passes the word into medieval French.
items.cn: tragique 把这个词带入中世纪法语。

items.en: The adjective tragic appears in English drama.
items.cn: 形容词 tragique 在英语戏剧中首先出现。

items.en: The word widens to describe real disasters and sad losses.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词扩大到形容真实的灾难和令人惋惜的损失。

note.en: Tragic is a theatre word that now names real disasters, and it sits near tragedy, comedy, and tragicomic.
note.cn: tragic 原本是剧场用语，如今用来指真实的灾难，与 tragedy、comedy、tragicomic 关系密切。

entries.definition: a very sad event or a serious play
entries.definitionCN: 悲剧；惨事

entries.definition: in a way that causes great sadness
entries.definitionCN: 悲惨地

entries.definition: both sad and funny at once
entries.definitionCN: 悲喜交加的

entries.definition: funny or relating to comedy
entries.definitionCN: 喜剧的；滑稽的（与 tragic 相对，并非同源）

entries.definition: feeling or showing unhappiness
entries.definitionCN: 难过的；悲伤的（日常用词，语气轻）

entries.definition: causing great damage or shock
entries.definitionCN: 毁灭性的；毁灭人心的（语气更重）

entries.definition: causing deep emotional pain
entries.definitionCN: 令人心碎的

normalIntro.en: Tragic wears the theatre mask: a serious fall that cannot be stopped, and the feeling it leaves behind.
normalIntro.cn: tragic 戴着剧场面具：一场无法阻止的严肃坠落，以及它留下的悲伤。

normal.en: The noun tragedy gives the adjective tragic.
normal.cn: 名词 tragedy 派生出形容词 tragic。

normal.en: A tragic accident is one with death or lasting injury.
normal.cn: a tragic accident 就是带死亡或永久伤害的事故。

normal.en: A tragic hero falls through a tragic flaw.
normal.cn: 悲剧英雄因一处「悲剧性缺陷」而坠落。

normal.en: The adverb tragically marks how a sad event happened.
normal.cn: 副词 tragically 说明悲惨事件发生的方式。

normal.en: Compare comedy: comic is funny, tragic is deeply sad.
normal.cn: 对比 comedy：comic 是好笑，tragic 是深深的悲伤。

abstract.en: Picture a broken bridge over a dark river.
abstract.cn: 想象一座横跨暗色河流的断桥。

abstract.en: See two masks on a stage, one smiling and one weeping.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上一副面具在笑，另一副在哭。

abstract.en: Think of a good plan failing on its last step.
abstract.cn: 想象一个周密的计划在最后一步落空。

examples.en: Firefighters died in the tragic blaze at the factory.
examples.cn: 消防员在那场工厂的惨烈大火中牺牲。

examples.en: Many tragic plays end with a hero facing his fate.
examples.cn: 许多悲剧的结尾是主人公面对自己的命运。

examples.en: It is tragic that the young musician never heard her own work performed.
examples.cn: 那位年轻音乐家从未听过自己的作品被演奏，令人惋惜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹扎吉」——有人在台上吹了一记悲凉的调子，扎进人心，难怪悲惨；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 tragoidia（悲剧，一般认为与 tragos「山羊」有关，存疑）→ 形容词 tragikos → 拉丁语 tragicus → 法语 tragique → 英语 tragic，核心义「命运碾碎欢乐的严肃坠落」。

sensesIntro.en: Tragic runs from real disasters to the theatre form, to the sadness of unavoidable loss, to the hero flaw, and finally to a serious style.
sensesIntro.cn: tragic 从真实的灾难走到戏剧体裁，再到不可避免的失落之悲、英雄的缺陷，最后是严肃庄严的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stage mask whose joy is crushed by fate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被命运碾碎欢乐的舞台面具。

branches.en: Real disaster is the most common modern sense.
branches.cn: 真实的灾难是当代最常见的义项。

branches.en: The theatre sense keeps the original stage meaning.
branches.cn: 戏剧义项保留了最初的舞台含义。

branches.en: The tragic hero sense names a fatal flaw.
branches.cn: 悲剧英雄义项指一出致命缺陷。

branches.en: An unavoidable loss borrows the stage sorrow.
branches.cn: 无法避免的损失借用了舞台上的悲伤。

branches.en: Both the play and its formal style share one elevated manner.
branches.cn: 剧本与其庄严风格共享同一种崇高调性。

intro.en: Tragic is built on the Greek tragedy word, and its family in English is tragedy, tragically, and tragicomic.
intro.cn: tragic 建立在希腊语「悲剧」一词上，它在英语中的词族是 tragedy、tragically 与 tragicomic。

latinIntro.en: Latin tragicus and tragoedia carry the Greek stage word into later European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tragicus 与 tragoedia 把希腊语舞台词带入后来的欧洲语言。

items.meaningCN: 悲剧；一般认为与「山羊」有关
items.example: Tragoidia is the old name of the stage form.
items.exampleCN: tragoidia 是这种舞台形式古老的名字。

items.meaningCN: 山羊（与悲剧起源有关联的猜测）
items.example: Tragos appears in one account of the name.
items.exampleCN: tragos 出现在关于这一名称的一种解释中。

items.example: The suffix -ikos forms tragikos.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ikos 构成 tragikos。

items.example: Tragic keeps the theatre weight.
items.exampleCN: tragic 保留了剧场那种分量。

items.meaning: a sad event or a serious play
items.example: Tragedy names the loss itself.
items.exampleCN: tragedy 指损失本身。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms tragically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 tragically。

items.example: Tragically often opens a sad report.
items.exampleCN: tragically 常用来引出沉痛的报道。

items.example: The form tragi- joins comedy words.
items.exampleCN: 词首 tragi- 与喜剧词结合。

items.example: Together they build tragicomic.
items.exampleCN: 两者结合构成 tragicomic。

items.example: Tragicomic blends the two stage moods.
items.exampleCN: tragicomic 融合了舞台的两种情绪。

definition_zh: 有轨电车；（矿山的）矿车；吊车滑轨
definition_en: a vehicle driven by electricity that runs on rails in the street; also a small wagon used in mines
core_image: 一辆沿轨滑行的车厢：车轮卡在两条钢轨之间，顺着轨道走
scene: 清晨的城市还没完全醒来，钢轨上已经响起了车铃声。A packed tram rattled along the rails past the old market.
sceneCN: 这里 tram 是「有轨电车」（第 1 个义项：在街道轨道上行驶的电力车辆）；句意：一辆挤满人的有轨电车沿着轨道叮当作响地驶过旧市场。

derivatives.zh: tram 与 way 合成，义为「电车轨道；有轨电车线路」
tram 与 line 合成，义为「电线线路；有轨车道」
tram 与 car 合成，义为「电车车厢；（矿）斗车」
tram 与 road 合成，义为「轨道；运矿车道」

senses.title: An electric streetcar on rails
senses.definition: a passenger vehicle powered by electricity that runs on rails laid in a street
senses.definitionCN: 铺设在街道上的钢轨上行驶的电力载客车辆
senses.example: We took the tram to the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 我们坐有轨电车去了博物馆。
senses.why: The short form of tramway began in mining tracks, and when electric cars ran on city rails the word moved onto the street.
senses.whyCN: tram 原本是 tramway（运矿轨道）的简称，当电车在城市钢轨上行驶时，这个词就走上了街道。

senses.title: A coal wagon in a mine
senses.definition: a small four wheeled wagon that carries coal or ore along rails in a mine
senses.definitionCN: 在矿井轨道上运送煤或矿石的四轮小车
senses.example: Workers pushed a loaded tram out of the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把装满的矿车推出隧道。
senses.why: Mining came first: a low wagon running along a wooden or iron track was the original tram.
senses.whyCN: 矿车才是最早的来源：沿着木制或铁制轨道滑行的矮小车斗，就是最初的 tram。

senses.title: A trolley hanging from a wire
senses.definition: a small carriage hung from a wire cable and used to carry goods or people over rough ground
senses.definitionCN: 悬挂在钢丝绳上的小车，用于在崎岖地面运送货物或人
senses.example: A wire tram carried the bags up the slope.
senses.exampleCN: 一架索道吊车把行李运上了斜坡。
senses.why: The core idea is a car sliding along a fixed track, and a wire cable gives the same sliding path in the air.
senses.whyCN: 核心想法是沿固定轨道滑动的车斗，而钢丝绳在空中提供了同样的滑行通道。

senses.title: The rails themselves
senses.definition: the set of rails on which a tram runs, used in the phrase tram rails
senses.definitionCN: 有轨电车行驶的钢轨组合，常见于 tram rails 之类的说法
senses.example: Rain gleamed on the tram rails in the street.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后的电车轨道在街面上发亮。
senses.why: Because the word named the whole track line before it named the car, the rails can still be called the tram.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词先指整条轨道、后指车辆，钢轨本身仍然可以被称作 tram。

senses.title: A hand pulled cart in a mill
senses.definition: a simple hand pulled cart on a short track, once used in mills and factories
senses.definitionCN: 在短轨上用手拉动的简易小车，旧时用于磨坊和工厂
senses.example: The old mill still has a rusting tram near the door.
senses.exampleCN: 老磨坊门旁还停着一辆生锈的运料车。
senses.why: Before streetcars, any little rail car in industry was a tram, and the hand pulled cart kept the name longest.
senses.whyCN: 在电车出现之前，工业里任何小型轨车都叫 tram，而手推车把这个名字保留得最久。

intro.en: Tram is a shortening of tramway and tramroad, mining terms of uncertain origin, perhaps from a German source.
intro.cn: tram 是 tramway 与 tramroad 的缩写，属于矿用术语，词源存疑，一般认为来自德语来源。

items.en: Tramway first names a rail line laid for wagons.
items.cn: tramway 最初指为货车铺设的轨道。

items.en: One account links tram to traam, a beam, but this is not certain.
items.cn: 一种说法认为 tram 与德语 traam（横梁）有关，但并不确定。

items.en: Tram shortens tramway and names the coal wagon.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语中 tram 缩短自 tramway，指运煤车斗。

items.en: American use applies the word to street railways.
items.cn: 美国用法把这个词用于城市街面铁路。

items.en: The electric streetcar becomes the ordinary meaning.
items.cn: 有轨电车成为最普通的含义。

items.en: British cities revive trams as a city transport choice.
items.cn: 英国城市重新把电车当作城市交通工具。

note.en: Tram is a rail word; its family is built by compounding with way, line, car, and road, and it sits near other public transport words.
note.cn: tram 是轨道类词语，其词族由 way、line、car、road 等复合而成，并与公共交通词语相邻。

entries.definition: a track or route for trams
entries.definitionCN: 电车轨道；电车路线

entries.definition: a tram or the wagon of a tram train
entries.definitionCN: 电车；矿斗车

entries.definition: a line of rails for trams
entries.definitionCN: 电车轨道；电车线路

entries.definition: to walk with heavy steps, or a person who wanders
entries.definitionCN: 重步走；流浪者（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: an electric vehicle on rails in the street
entries.definitionCN: 有轨电车（美国常用说法）

entries.definition: a bus powered by wires above the road
entries.definitionCN: 无轨电车（有电杆但无钢轨）

entries.definition: a modern urban rail system, often using trams
entries.definitionCN: 轻轨（现代城市轨道系统）

normalIntro.en: Tram is a car on a fixed line: from a mine wagon to a street streetcar, it always follows rails.
normalIntro.cn: tram 是沿着固定线路走的车：无论从矿车变成街头电车，它始终跟着轨道。

normal.en: The base word grew from tramway, so tram and way belong together.
normal.cn: 这个词从 tramway 缩来，所以 tram 与 way 天生是一对。

normal.en: A tram line is the track that keeps the car on course.
normal.cn: tram line 就是让电车保持在正确线路上的轨道。

normal.en: Tram stop is where the car stops to let people on.
normal.cn: tram stop 就是电车停下让人上车的地方。

normal.en: Take the tram, not the bus, when the rails are near.
normal.cn: 轨道就在旁边时，就说 take the tram，而不是坐公交。

normal.en: Compare streetcar: it is the American word for the same thing.
normal.cn: 对比 streetcar：美国说法指的是同一种车。

abstract.en: Picture a bell ringing as two steel rails shine in rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨里两条钢轨发亮，铃声随之响起。

abstract.en: See a low wagon rolling out of a dark mine tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆矮矮的车斗从昏暗的矿道里滚出。

abstract.en: Think of a small carriage hanging from a wire over a steep slope.
abstract.cn: 想象陡坡上空有一根钢丝绳，挂着一辆小车斗。

examples.en: The tram was so full that we had to stand.
examples.cn: 电车上挤得满满当当，我们只好站着。

examples.en: Mining trams carried coal to the surface in wooden cars.
examples.cn: 矿车把煤从井下运到地面，车厢是木制的。

examples.en: The new tram line connects the station with the university.
examples.cn: 新的电车线路把火车站和大学连接起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿么」——电车在街中央「穿」行而过，沿着钢轨一路顺溜地溜过去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 tramway、tramroad（运矿轨道）→ 十九世纪缩写为 tram 指矿车 → 十九世纪后期扩展为街面车 → 现代指有轨电车；词源存疑，一般认为与德语 traam（横梁，存疑）有关。

sensesIntro.en: Tram began as a mining wagon, then the word moved onto urban rails, and finally expanded to cable cars and hand carts.
sensesIntro.cn: tram 最初指矿车，随后这个词转到城市钢轨上，最后扩展到索道车与手推料车。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small car riding two fixed rails.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆卡在两条固定钢轨上的小车。

branches.en: The city streetcar is the everyday modern sense.
branches.cn: 城市有轨电车是当代日常义项。

branches.en: The mine wagon keeps the oldest industrial sense.
branches.cn: 矿车保留了最古老的工业义项。

branches.en: A hanging cable car is the overhead extension.
branches.cn: 悬挂索道车是架空的延伸。

branches.en: The rails are named after the car that runs on them.
branches.cn: 钢轨以在其上行驶的车来命名。

branches.en: Both a mine wagon and a mill cart follow a fixed short track.
branches.cn: 矿车与磨坊料车都沿着固定的短轨行驶。

intro.en: Tram is a short English base that mostly builds compounds, as in tramway, tramline, tramcar, and tramroad.
intro.cn: tram 是一个简短的英语基础词，主要通过复合构词，如 tramway、tramline、tramcar 与 tramroad。

latinIntro.en: Tram has no certain Latin root; a German word for a beam is sometimes suggested, but this is not settled.
latinIntro.cn: tram 没有确定的拉丁语词根；有时被推测与德语表示横梁的词有关，但尚无定论。

items.meaning: a rail car for people or coal
items.example: Tram is the short base word.
items.exampleCN: tram 是这一词族简短的基础词。

items.meaningCN: 表示道路或路线的词尾
items.example: The form -way builds tramway.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -way 构成 tramway。

items.example: A tramway ran beside the canal.
items.exampleCN: 运河边曾有一条电车轨道。

items.meaning: a route or a row of rails
items.meaningCN: 表示线路或轨道的词尾
items.example: The form -line builds tramline.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -line 构成 tramline。

items.example: The tramline crosses the square.
items.exampleCN: 电车轨道穿过广场。

items.meaningCN: 表示车辆或车厢的词尾
items.example: The form -car builds tramcar.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -car 构成 tramcar。

items.example: A tramcar swayed through the narrow street.
items.exampleCN: 一节电车车厢摇晃着穿过窄街。

items.example: The form -road builds tramroad.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -road 构成 tramroad。

items.example: A wooden tramroad led to the pit.
items.exampleCN: 一条木制运矿车道通向矿坑。

items.meaning: the rail pair a tram runs on
items.example: The tram-track glinted after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后电车双轨闪着光。

definition_zh: 流浪汉；长途跋涉；重脚步声；徒步穿越
definition_en: a person with no home who walks from place to place, or a long tiring walk with heavy steps
core_image: 一个人背着旧铺盖，脚步沉重地从一个镇走到另一个镇
scene: 雨夜的车站长椅上，蜷着一个浑身湿透的流浪汉。A wet tramp huddled on the bench of the station at night.
sceneCN: 这里 tramp 是「流浪汉」（第 1 个义项：居无定所、徒步漂泊的人）；句意：雨夜里，一个浑身湿透的流浪汉蜷在车站长椅上。

pos.zh: 长途跋涉；沉重的脚步声
拖着沉重的脚步走；徒步穿越
踏着走过；徒步穿越某地

collocations.zh: 一个无家可归的流浪汉

derivatives.zh: 动词 tramp 去 e 加 -er 构成，指「徒步旅行者」
动词 tramp 加 -ing 名词化，指「长途徒步」
与 tramp 只是拼写相近，词源一般认为来自意大利语，并非派生关系

senses.title: A homeless wanderer
senses.definition: a person who has no home or job and walks from place to place
senses.definitionCN: 没有家或工作、从一处徒步漂泊到另一处的人
senses.example: An old tramp asked us for a cup of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 一个老流浪汉向我们讨了一杯茶。
senses.why: The core image of heavy walking without a destination turned into the name of the person who walks that way.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「无目的地沉重行走」，走动的人就被直接叫作 tramp，人的称呼由动作转来。

senses.title: A long tiring walk
senses.definition: a long walk over difficult ground, often with heavy steps
senses.definitionCN: 在难走的路上进行的长时间步行，常伴着沉重的脚步
senses.example: We went on a ten-kilometre tramp across the moors.
senses.exampleCN: 我们穿过荒原徒步了十公里。
senses.why: The act of wandering became a countable journey named after its heavy, steady rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 「流浪」这一动作被具体化为一次可数的行程，得名于那种沉重而稳定的节奏。

senses.title: The sound of heavy steps
senses.definition: the loud sound made by heavy boots or feet walking
senses.definitionCN: 沉重靴子或脚步走动时发出的响亮声音
senses.example: I heard the tramp of boots outside the door.
senses.exampleCN: 我听见门外有靴子沉重的脚步声。
senses.why: The same heavy walking is heard as a sound, so the word names the noise as well as the action.
senses.whyCN: 同样的沉重行走被耳朵听见，于是这个词也从动作转为指那种沉闷的声音。

senses.title: To walk with heavy steps
senses.definition: to walk steadily and loudly, especially for a long distance
senses.definitionCN: 步伐沉重而响亮地走，尤指走很长的路
senses.example: She tramped up the stairs in her wet boots.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着湿靴子噔噔地走上楼梯。
senses.why: As a verb the word keeps the onomatopoeic thud of boots hitting the ground.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，词里保留了拟声感，像靴子一下下砸在地面上。

senses.title: To cover a place on foot
senses.definition: to walk across or over a large area, often for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 徒步穿行或走遍一大片地方，往往历时很久
senses.example: They tramped the whole forest looking for the lost dog.
senses.exampleCN: 他们踏遍整片树林寻找走失的狗。
senses.why: Walking without a fixed route extends to covering ground thoroughly on foot, including searching.
senses.whyCN: 没有固定路线的行走，延伸为用双脚把一片地方走遍，也包括为了搜寻而踏遍。

intro.en: Tramp is probably of Germanic origin, related to words for stamping; the spelling and the sense of heavy walking are recorded from the Middle English period.
intro.cn: tramp 一般认为源于日耳曼语，与表示「重踏」的词同源；其拼写与「沉重行走」义在中古英语时期已有记录。

items.en: Related forms in Low German and Dutch mean to stamp or trudge.
items.cn: 低地德语和荷兰语中的同族词意为「重踏、跋涉」。这是重构与同源比较的结论，并非直接借用。

items.en: A verb meaning to walk heavily appears in the written record.
items.cn: 中古英语记录中出现表示「沉重地走」的动词。

items.en: The noun develops from the act of tramping to the person who tramps.
items.cn: 名词由「徒步跋涉」这一动作，转而指做这种动作的人。

items.en: Tramp comes to name homeless wanderers and the sound of marching feet.
items.cn: 词义扩展到流浪汉，以及行进脚步发出的声音。

items.en: The verb is widely used for long hill walks and for walking across a place.
items.cn: 现代英语中该动词广泛用于山间长途徒步，以及「走遍某地」。

note.en: Tramp is close to trample and trample-related verbs in shape, and to vagrant and drifter in meaning.
note.cn: tramp 在形态上贴近 trample 等表示「重踏」的词，在意义上贴近 vagrant、drifter 等表示「漂泊者」的词。

entries.definition: to step heavily on something and crush it
entries.definitionCN: 踩踏、践踏（与 tramp 同源于「重踏」，但强调压坏东西）

entries.definition: a person who tramps over country
entries.definitionCN: 徒步旅行者，由动词 tramp 加 -er 构成

entries.definition: a springy sheet used for jumping
entries.definitionCN: 蹦床，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a person without a settled home or job
entries.definitionCN: 流浪者，措辞更正式，常带法律色彩

entries.definition: a person who moves around without a plan
entries.definitionCN: 漂泊者，强调漫无目的

entries.definition: a long walk in the countryside
entries.definitionCN: 远足、徒步，多指有计划的休闲步行

normalIntro.en: Tramp sounds like boots hitting a hard road: one heavy step after another, for a long way.
normalIntro.cn: tramp 听起来像靴子砸在硬路上：一步接一步，走得很远。

normal.en: A tramp is a person, so you can say an old tramp came to the door.
normal.cn: tramp 可指人：an old tramp 就是一位老流浪汉。

normal.en: Tramp as a noun also names a long walk: go on a tramp.
normal.cn: 作名词还可指长途徒步：go on a tramp。

normal.en: The tramp of boots is a sound, not a person.
normal.cn: the tramp of boots 指声音，不是人。

normal.en: As a verb it takes through or across: tramp through the woods.
normal.cn: 作动词常与 through 或 across 连用：tramp through the woods。

normal.en: Compare trample: trample crushes things underfoot, tramp just walks heavily.
normal.cn: 对比 trample：trample 是把东西踩坏，tramp 只是沉重地走。

abstract.en: Picture a worn boot in the mud, with no road ahead.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沾满泥的旧靴子，前方没有路。

abstract.en: Hear a slow thud, thud, thud along an empty street.
abstract.cn: 想象空街上一声接一声的沉闷脚步。

abstract.en: See a long line of footprints crossing a field at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时一串长长的脚印穿过田野。

examples.en: The tramp had walked thirty miles before sunset.
examples.cn: 那个流浪汉在日落前走了三十英里。

examples.en: We tramped all day through the muddy valley.
examples.cn: 我们一整天跋涉在泥泞的山谷里。

examples.en: The tramp of hooves could be heard from the yard.
examples.cn: 院子里能听见沉重的蹄声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蹋·搬」——挨户「搬」家、脚「蹋」泥路，就是流浪汉的日子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: tramp 一般认为源自日耳曼语系，与低地德语、荷兰语中表示「重踏、跋涉」的词同源（同源比较，非直接借词）；由「沉重地走」发展出「流浪汉」「长途跋涉」「脚步声」等义，与 trample 共享「踩踏」意象。

sensesIntro.en: Tramp starts from heavy walking on foot, then names the person who wanders, the journey, the sound, and finally the act of covering ground.
sensesIntro.cn: tramp 从「沉重地走」出发，先指这样走的人，再指这趟行程、脚步的声音，最后指走遍某地的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: heavy boots step by step along a road with no home at the end.
core.cn: 核心意象：沉重的靴子一步一步走在路上，路的尽头没有家。

branches.en: The wanderer is the person made from the action.
branches.cn: 流浪汉是把动作转指人。

branches.en: The journey is the action counted as a trip.
branches.cn: 长途跋涉是把动作当成一次行程来数。

branches.en: The sound is the walk heard with the ears.
branches.cn: 脚步声是用耳朵听到的行走。

branches.en: The verb preserves the original heavy gait.
branches.cn: 动词保留了最初的那种沉重步态。

branches.en: Walking without a fixed road grows into walking across a whole area.
branches.cn: 没有固定路线的走，扩展为走遍一整片地方。

intro.en: Tramp is a word of Germanic stock, so its English family is small: tramper and tramping, plus the related trample.
intro.cn: tramp 属于日耳曼语来源的词，英语词族不大：加上 -er、-ing 构成 tramper、tramping，另有同源的 trample。

latinIntro.en: Tramp has no Latin source and no Latin relatives; its nearest relatives belong to the Germanic word for stamping.
latinIntro.cn: tramp 没有拉丁语来源，也没有拉丁同族词；它最相近的同族词属于日耳曼语中表示「重踏」的那一组。

items.example: They tramped across the moor.
items.exampleCN: 他们踏过荒原。

items.example: A tramp knocked at the farm door.
items.exampleCN: 一个流浪汉敲了农场大门。

items.example: Tramper is built with -er.
items.exampleCN: tramper 由 -er 构成。

items.example: Trampers often carry light packs.
items.exampleCN: 远足者常背轻便行囊。

items.example: Tramping is the activity noun.
items.exampleCN: tramping 是表示活动的名词。

items.example: Tramping is popular in hill country.
items.exampleCN: 山地间徒步很受欢迎。

items.example: Trample names repeated stamping.
items.exampleCN: trample 表示反复踩踏。

items.example: Do not trample the young grass.
items.exampleCN: 不要踩坏嫩草。

items.meaning: a cargo ship calling at any port
items.example: A tramp steamer sails wherever freight waits.
items.exampleCN: 不定航线货船哪里等货就开往哪里。

definition_zh: 平静的；安宁的；镇定的；风平浪静的
definition_en: calm and quiet, free from worry, noise or disturbance
core_image: 无风的正午，湖面像一面镜子，连一丝波纹都没有
scene: 湖面像一面镜子，岸边的柳树一动不动，连风都停了。The lake was tranquil in the early morning, without a single ripple.
sceneCN: 这里 tranquil 是「平静的」（第 1 个义项：没有风浪、没有噪音的安静）；句意：清晨的湖面很平静，没有一丝波纹。

derivatives.zh: 形容词 tranquil 去 l 加 -ity 构成，指「宁静；安宁」
英式拼写，-ll- 双写，义同 tranquility
tranquil 加 -l- 与 -ize 构成的英式拼写，义同 tranquilize
tranquil 加 -ize 构成，指「使镇静」

senses.title: Calm and free from disturbance
senses.definition: quiet and still, with no noise, movement or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 安静而静止，没有噪音、动静或麻烦
senses.example: We spent a tranquil afternoon by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河边度过了一个宁静的下午。
senses.why: The Latin root means quiet, and the first sense is this quietness felt as calm still air or water.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根本义就是「安静」，这个义项是安静直接落在水面、空气或环境上的样子。

senses.title: Free from worry
senses.definition: peaceful in feeling, with no anxiety or upset
senses.definitionCN: 心情平和，没有焦虑或不安
senses.example: After the exam she felt tranquil for the first time in weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 考试结束后，她几周来第一次感到安宁。
senses.why: A still surface becomes a still mind: outer quiet is used to describe the inner life.
senses.whyCN: 平静的水面被借来形容平静的心：外部之静扩展到内心世界，指无忧无虑。

senses.title: Calm under pressure
senses.definition: remaining calm when a person is tested or upset
senses.definitionCN: 在受到考验或激怒时仍保持冷静
senses.example: He gave a tranquil reply even when the crowd shouted at him.
senses.exampleCN: 即使人群对他大喊，他的回答仍然镇定自若。
senses.why: From the state of quiet comes the ability to stay quiet, which is calm self control.
senses.whyCN: 从「处于安静中」引申出「能够保持安静」，也就是临事不乱的镇定。

senses.title: Of water, weather or air
senses.definition: not windy, rough or choppy, said of the sea, sky or air
senses.definitionCN: 用于海、天空或空气，指没有风浪、不翻涌
senses.example: The sea looked tranquil just before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，海面看起来风平浪静。
senses.why: The most literal sense is still kept for nature, where calm can be seen and measured.
senses.whyCN: 最字面的义项留给了自然：风浪可以被看见、被测量，所以用于水和天气最直接。

senses.title: Serene in appearance
senses.definition: looking calm and gentle in face or manner, without strong feeling shown
senses.definitionCN: 神情或举止安详温和，不显露强烈情绪
senses.example: Her tranquil smile made the whole room feel softer.
senses.exampleCN: 她安详的微笑让整个房间都柔和起来。
senses.why: Quiet, when worn by a face, becomes the look of a person at peace.
senses.whyCN: 安静挂在脸上，就成了一个心平气和的人所显露的安详神情。

intro.en: Tranquil comes from Latin tranquillus, still and quiet, probably built from trans, beyond, and a root for quiet; the English form was shaped during the Renaissance by Latin and French models.
intro.cn: tranquil 来自拉丁语 tranquillus（静止、安静），一般认为由 trans（越过）与表示「安静」的词根构成；英语形式在文艺复兴时期依拉丁语和法语模型定型。

items.en: Tranquillus means still, calm and undisturbed.
items.cn: tranquillus 意为静止的、平静的、不受扰动的。

items.en: Tranquillitas names the state of calm, and tranquillare is to make calm.
items.cn: tranquillitas 指平静的状态，tranquillare 意为使平静。

items.en: The form passes north of the Alps as tranquil or tranquille.
items.cn: 这一词形越过阿尔卑斯山传入古法语，写作 tranquil 或 tranquille，一般认为如此。

items.en: Tranquil enters written English, often of the sea, weather and mind.
items.cn: tranquil 进入书面英语，常用来描写海、天气和心境。

items.en: Spelling settles with one l in American usage, while British English keeps tranquillity with two.
items.cn: 现代英语中，美式拼写只有一个 l，而英式 tranquillity 仍保留双 l。

note.en: Tranquil is a near relative of calm and serene, and word family member of tranquillity and tranquilize.
note.cn: tranquil 与 calm、serene 意义相近，与 tranquillity、tranquilize 属同一词族。

entries.definition: the state of being calm and quiet
entries.definitionCN: 宁静、安宁，由 tranquil 构成的名词

entries.definition: calmness and peace
entries.definitionCN: 安宁、平静，英式拼写双写 l

entries.definition: to make calm, often with medicine
entries.definitionCN: 使镇静，常指用药物镇静

entries.definition: not worried, excited or rough
entries.definitionCN: 平静的、冷静的，最常用，可指人和天气

entries.definition: calm and untroubled in a bright, clear way
entries.definitionCN: 安详的、宁静的，偏文学，带光明的宁静感

entries.definition: full of peace, without war or noise
entries.definitionCN: 和平的、安静的，侧重没有冲突或噪音

normalIntro.en: Tranquil may relate to trans, across, plus a root for quiet: quiet that runs all the way through.
normalIntro.cn: tranquil 一般认为与 trans（越过）相关，加表示「安静」的词根：一种从头到尾都安静的状态。

normal.en: Tranquil is usually a written word for pleasant quiet, not for a crowd.
normal.cn: tranquil 多用于书面语，带愉悦感的安静，不用于人群。

normal.en: The noun is tranquillity in British spelling and tranquility in American.
normal.cn: 名词英式写作 tranquillity，美式写作 tranquility。

normal.en: The verb tranquilize adds -ize and means to make calm.
normal.cn: 动词 tranquilize 加 -ize，意为使平静；tranquilizer 是镇静剂。

normal.en: The adjective pattern is the same as quiet, so we say a tranquil place, not a tranquil noise.
normal.cn: 形容词用法与 quiet 相似：可以说 a tranquil place，不说 a tranquil noise。

normal.en: Compare calm: calm can describe a person in any situation, tranquil sounds more peaceful and literary.
normal.cn: 对比 calm：calm 可形容任何情境下的人，tranquil 更宁静、更书面。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror-still lake at dawn, not one ripple.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时如镜的湖面，一丝波纹也没有。

abstract.en: Imagine a white sail hanging still on a windless sea.
abstract.cn: 想象无风的海面上，一张白帆静静地垂着。

abstract.en: Think of a person breathing slowly in a quiet garden.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在安静的花园里慢慢呼吸。

examples.en: The village is tranquil in winter, with almost no visitors.
examples.cn: 村子在冬天十分宁静，几乎没有访客。

examples.en: She kept a tranquil face while the argument went on.
examples.cn: 争论持续时，她一直保持安详的神情。

examples.en: A tranquil sea is a good sign for small boats.
examples.cn: 平静的海面对小船来说是好兆头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「圈·静」——像一个「圈」起来的湖面，「静」得没有一点波；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tranquillus（静止的、平静的），一般认为由 trans（越过）加表示「安静」的词根构成，词源细节存疑；经古法语 tranquil（le）进入英语，核心义一直是「无扰动的平静」。

sensesIntro.en: Tranquil is calm rooted in still water: it first describes still places, then unworried minds, then the calm a person shows under pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: tranquil 的「平静」根植于静止的水：先描写安静的地方，再描写无忧的心境，最后描写人在压力下的镇定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror-still lake with no ripple and no wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：无风无浪、像镜子一样的湖面。

branches.en: The still place is the first and most common sense.
branches.cn: 静止的地方是最先出现、最常用的义项。

branches.en: The still mind borrows the image from water.
branches.cn: 平静的心借用了水面的意象。

branches.en: Staying calm is quiet held under pressure.
branches.cn: 镇定是压力之下仍守住的安静。

branches.en: Water and weather keep the most literal sense.
branches.cn: 水和天气保留最字面的平静义。

branches.en: A serene face is peace made visible.
branches.cn: 安详的神情是内心宁静的外露。

intro.en: Tranquil has a Latin base, so its English family uses -ity, -ize and -ly, plus the -quill- core seen in several related words.
intro.cn: tranquil 有拉丁语基础，英语词族用 -ity、-ize、-ly 派生，核心部分是 -quill-，也见于若干相关词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tranquillus and tranquillitas directly supply the adjective and the noun in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tranquillus 与 tranquillitas 直接提供了英语的形容词与名词。

items.example: The garden is tranquil at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 傍晚的花园十分宁静。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms a state noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成表示状态的名词。

items.example: Tranquility is the American spelling.
items.exampleCN: tranquility 是美式拼写。

items.example: Tranquillity keeps the double l.
items.exampleCN: tranquillity 保留双写 l。

items.example: The suffix -ize makes tranquilize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 tranquilize。

items.example: They tranquilize the injured animal.
items.exampleCN: 他们给受伤的动物注射镇静剂。

items.example: The suffix -izer makes tranquilizer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -izer 构成 tranquilizer。

items.example: The vet used a tranquilizer.
items.exampleCN: 兽医用了镇静剂。

items.example: The suffix -ly makes tranquilly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 tranquilly。

items.example: The river flowed tranquilly.
items.exampleCN: 河水静静地流着。

items.example: The root element -quill- is old and of uncertain form.
items.exampleCN: 词根要素 -quill- 年代久远，具体形态存疑。

definition_zh: 宁静；安宁；平和的心境
definition_en: the state of being calm, quiet and free from disturbance
core_image: 清晨没有风的海面，浪花全停，天地之间一片安静
scene: 山谷里只听得见溪水声，远处的寺庙被薄雾包着。She found genuine tranquility in the quiet monastery.
sceneCN: 这里 tranquility 是「宁静」（第 1 个义项：环境安静、不受打扰的状态）；句意：她在安静的修道院里找到了真正的宁静。

derivatives.zh: 名词 tranquility 去 -ity 还原的形容词，指「平静的」
同词族动词，tranquil 加 -ize，指「使镇静」
同词族副词，指「宁静地」
tranquil 加 -ness 构成的另一名词形式，义近但少用

senses.title: Freedom from noise and disturbance
senses.definition: a state in which a place is quiet and disturbed by nothing
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方安静、没有受到任何打扰的状态
senses.example: The old library is a place of great tranquility.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老图书馆是个极其宁静的地方。
senses.why: The Latin noun tranquillitas names a still state, and here the stillness belongs to a place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tranquillitas 指「静止的状态」，这个义项把静止落在了一个地方上。

senses.title: Peace of mind
senses.definition: the calm feeling of a mind free from worry or anger
senses.definitionCN: 心灵摆脱忧虑或愤怒后的平静感受
senses.example: Meditation brought her a deep sense of tranquility.
senses.exampleCN: 冥想带给她一种深沉的内心平静。
senses.why: The still surface of water is turned inward, so the noun also names the still state of a mind.
senses.whyCN: 如静水般的表面转向内心，名词也用来指心灵静止的状态，也就是内心的平静。

senses.title: Public order and peace
senses.definition: the condition of a country or community being calm and orderly
senses.definitionCN: 国家或社区安定有序、没有动荡的状况
senses.example: The new laws restored tranquility to the streets.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律让街道恢复了安宁。
senses.why: Stillness scaled up to a whole community becomes social peace and public order.
senses.whyCN: 把静止放大到整个社会，就变成了公共秩序与社会安宁。

senses.title: Still water or air
senses.definition: the calm condition of the sea, sky or air when nothing moves
senses.definitionCN: 海面、天空或空气一动不动时的平静状态
senses.example: The tranquility of the sea surprised the sailors.
senses.exampleCN: 海面的风平浪静让水手们很惊讶。
senses.why: The literal state of still nature is where the word began and is still kept.
senses.whyCN: 自然界的静止状态正是这个词的起点，至今仍保留为最字面的义项。

senses.title: A calm and steady manner
senses.definition: calm behaviour and a gentle manner shown by a person
senses.definitionCN: 一个人表现出的从容举止和温和态度
senses.example: She answered the reporters with perfect tranquility.
senses.exampleCN: 她十分从容地回答了记者的问题。
senses.why: The inner calm shows on the outside, becoming the visible quality of how a person behaves.
senses.whyCN: 内心的平静外显出来，就变成一个人举止上的从容，可以被旁人看见。

intro.en: Tranquility is the Latin noun tranquillitas, calmness, taken into English through Latin models; British English keeps the double l in tranquillity.
intro.cn: tranquility 是拉丁语名词 tranquillitas（平静）经拉丁语模型进入英语的结果；英式英语写作 tranquillity，保留双写 l。

items.en: Tranquillus means still and calm, often of the sea and the mind.
items.cn: tranquillus 意为静止、平静，常用来形容海和心境。

items.en: The abstract noun tranquillitas names the state of being calm.
items.cn: 抽象名词 tranquillitas 指平静的状态。

items.en: Medieval Latin and French forms carry the noun towards English.
items.cn: 中古拉丁语和法语的形式把这个名词带向英语。

items.en: The noun enters English and is used for peace of the sea and of the mind.
items.cn: 该名词进入英语，用来指海面的平静与心境的平和。

items.en: American spelling simplifies the double l to tranquility.
items.cn: 现代美式拼写把双写 l 简化为单写 l，即 tranquility。

note.en: Tranquility pairs with tranquil as its noun, and stands close to peace and calm in meaning.
note.cn: tranquility 是 tranquil 的名词形式，意义上与 peace、calm 相近。

entries.definition: calm and quiet
entries.definitionCN: 平静的、宁静的，是这个词的形容词

entries.definition: calm and peace
entries.definitionCN: 安宁，英式拼写双写 l

entries.definition: to make calm or sleepy with medicine
entries.definitionCN: 使镇静，常指用药

entries.definition: freedom from war, noise or upset
entries.definitionCN: 和平、安宁，范围更广，也可指没有战争

entries.definition: a quiet, unworried state
entries.definitionCN: 平静，多作形容词，作名词时偏口语

entries.definition: a clear and deep calmness
entries.definitionCN: 安详，偏文学，带明亮、清朗的平静

normalIntro.en: Tranquility is the noun for the adjective tranquil: take tranquil, drop the l and add -ity.
normalIntro.cn: tranquility 是形容词 tranquil 的名词：去掉 l，加上 -ity。

normal.en: Tranquility is the American spelling, tranquillity the British one.
normal.cn: 美式写作 tranquility，英式写作 tranquillity。

normal.en: It is uncountable in most uses, so we say peace and tranquility, not a tranquility.
normal.cn: 多数情况下不可数：peace and tranquility，不说 a tranquility。

normal.en: The phrase inner tranquility is common in mind and health writing.
normal.cn: inner tranquility 常见于心理与健康类文章。

normal.en: A haven of tranquility means a very quiet, safe place.
normal.cn: a haven of tranquility 指一处非常安静的避风港。

normal.en: Compare quiet: tranquility is a state, quiet can also be a piece of silence or a command.
normal.cn: 对比 quiet：tranquility 只表示状态，quiet 还可指一段安静或一声命令。

abstract.en: Picture a sea with no wind and no wave, like a sheet of glass.
abstract.cn: 想象无风无浪的海面，像一块玻璃。

abstract.en: Hear the last sound fade in an empty valley.
abstract.cn: 想象空谷里最后一点回声消散。

abstract.en: Think of breathing out slowly and feeling the whole body settle.
abstract.cn: 想象慢慢呼气，整个身体都安定下来。

examples.en: The garden offers a rare tranquility in the middle of the city.
examples.cn: 这座花园在城中心提供了一份难得的宁静。

examples.en: He described the tranquility of the mountain lake in his diary.
examples.cn: 他在日记里描写了山间湖泊的宁静。

examples.en: After retirement she found tranquility in painting.
examples.cn: 退休后她在绘画中找到了安宁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿·快·离」——穿过喧闹，快些离开，就能得到安宁；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tranquillus（平静的）加名词后缀 -itas 构成 tranquillitas（平静状态），经中古拉丁语与法语进入英语；与 tranquil、tranquilize 同根，核心是 -quill-「安静」，细节存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Tranquility names the state behind tranquil: first a quiet place, then a quiet mind, then peace in society, water and manner.
sensesIntro.cn: tranquility 是 tranquil 背后的状态名词：先指安静的地方，再指安静的心，进而指社会、水面与举止上的安宁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a windless sea with no wave, wrapped in silence.
core.cn: 核心意象：无风无浪、被寂静包住的海面。

branches.en: The quiet place is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 安静的地方是最日常的义项。

branches.en: The quiet mind moves stillness inward.
branches.cn: 心灵的平静把静止转向内心。

branches.en: Public peace scales stillness up to a whole society.
branches.cn: 社会安宁把静态放大到全社会。

branches.en: Still water keeps the literal sense.
branches.cn: 静水保留了最字面的义项。

branches.en: A calm manner is tranquility made visible.
branches.cn: 从容的举止是宁静的外显。

intro.en: Tranquility is an -ity noun built on tranquil, and the family runs through tranquil, tranquilly, tranquilize and tranquilizer.
intro.cn: tranquility 是由 tranquil 加 -ity 构成的名词，词族包括 tranquil、tranquilly、tranquilize、tranquilizer。

latinIntro.en: Latin tranquillitas and tranquillus supply both the noun and the adjective, with tranquillare behind the verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tranquillitas 与 tranquillus 分别提供了名词与形容词，动词则来自 tranquillare。

items.example: The valley is tranquil at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 黎明时山谷很宁静。

items.example: The suffix -ity turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 把形容词变为名词。

items.example: Tranquility is the American spelling.
items.exampleCN: tranquility 是美式拼写。

items.example: Tranquillity is the British spelling.
items.exampleCN: tranquillity 是英式拼写。

items.example: The suffix -ly makes tranquilly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 tranquilly。

items.example: The boat moved tranquilly.
items.exampleCN: 船静静地移动。

items.example: The suffix -ize makes tranquilize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 tranquilize。

items.example: The keeper tranquilized the animal.
items.exampleCN: 饲养员把动物麻醉镇静了。

items.example: The nurse gave him a tranquilizer.
items.exampleCN: 护士给了他镇静剂。

items.example: The suffix -ness makes tranquilness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 tranquilness。

definition_zh: 抄写；把（讲话、录音）转写成文字；译写（乐谱）；标音；转录（基因信息）
definition_en: to write down something that is spoken or to copy information from one form into another, as written text, musical notes, phonetic symbols or data from a gene
core_image: 一段声音或一页原文被一个字一个字搬到另一张纸上，横着搬过去
scene: 研究者戴着耳机，把录音里每一句话逐字敲进文档。She spent the whole night transcribing the interviews word for word.
sceneCN: 这里 transcribe 是「把讲话转写成文字」（第 1 个义项：把说的话或录音逐字写成文字）；句意：她整夜都在逐字转写访谈录音。

pos.zh: 动词：抄写；转写；译写乐谱；标音

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「转写；文字稿；标音；转录」
由动词加表示「做……的人或工具」的后缀构成，义为「转写员；转录仪器」
同一词根的名词，义为「文字稿；成绩单；抄本」
由 transcript 加表示「酶」的后缀构成，义为「转录酶」

senses.title: To write down spoken words
senses.definition: to put speech, a recording or a broadcast into written form, word for word
senses.definitionCN: 把说话、录音或广播逐字写成文字
senses.example: She spent the whole night transcribing the interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 她整夜都在转写访谈内容。
senses.why: Latin trans- means across and scribere means to write, so the word pictures writing carried across from a voice to a page.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 trans- 表示「横越」，scribere 表示「写」；这个词的画面就是把文字从声音那一端搬到纸面上。

senses.title: To copy out a text
senses.definition: to copy written material over into another place or form, especially by hand
senses.definitionCN: 把书面材料复制到别处或改写成另一种形式，尤指手抄
senses.example: Monks transcribed these pages by candlelight.
senses.exampleCN: 修士们借着烛光抄写这些书页。
senses.why: The oldest use is the most literal one: writing carried across from an old copy to a new sheet, letter by letter.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法最直白：把旧抄本上的字一个字母一个字母地搬到新纸上。

senses.title: To set music in another form
senses.definition: to rewrite a piece of music for a different instrument or voice, or to write down a performance
senses.definitionCN: 把乐曲改写给别的乐器或人声演奏，或把演奏记成乐谱
senses.example: He transcribed the orchestral score for two guitars.
senses.exampleCN: 他把管弦乐总谱改编成两把吉他的版本。
senses.why: The same across-and-write image applies to sound: notes are taken out of one instrument and written again for another.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「跨越再书写」的画面用在声音上：音符从一种乐器取出，再为另一种乐器重新写一遍。

senses.title: To represent speech sounds
senses.definition: to represent sounds in phonetic symbols
senses.definitionCN: 用音标符号记录语音
senses.example: The dictionary transcribes each headword in IPA.
senses.exampleCN: 词典用国际音标符号转写每个词目。
senses.why: Sounds can also be written, so transcribing becomes the act of carrying an unworded sound across into symbols.
senses.whyCN: 声音也能被书写，于是 transcribe 就成了把没有文字的声音跨写成符号的动作。

senses.title: To copy genetic information
senses.definition: to make an RNA copy of a sequence of DNA
senses.definitionCN: 以一段 DNA 序列为模板合成 RNA 拷贝
senses.example: The cell transcribes the gene into messenger RNA.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞把该基因转录成信使 RNA。
senses.why: Molecular biology borrowed the word because information is again copied across from one medium to another, from DNA to RNA.
senses.whyCN: 分子生物学借用这个词，因为信息又一次从一种介质跨抄到另一种介质，即从 DNA 到 RNA。

senses.title: A transcriber in action
senses.titleCN: 转写员的做法：听写、标注
senses.definition: to work as a transcriber, listening closely and marking pauses and unclear words
senses.definitionCN: 充当转写员，仔细听辨并标出停顿与听不清的词
senses.example: Two assistants transcribed the tapes and checked each other.
senses.exampleCN: 两名助手转写了录音带并互相核对。
senses.why: As a job the verb names the steady craft of the same act: careful listening followed by writing that carries every word across.
senses.whyCN: 作为一项工作，动词指的正是同一动作的细致手艺：先仔细听，再把每个词搬写到纸面。

intro.en: Transcribe joins Latin trans-, across, with the verb scribere, to write, and reaches English through Medieval Latin transcribere and transscribere.
intro.cn: transcribe 由拉丁语前缀 trans-（横越）与动词 scribere（书写）构成，经中世纪拉丁语 transcribere、transscribere 进入英语。

items.en: The root behind scribere and Greek graphein, meaning to scratch or engrave, is generally reconstructed as *sker-, to cut. The deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为 scribere 与希腊语 graphein 背后的词根为 *sker-，意为「刻、划」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Scribo, scribere, scripsi, scriptum meant to draw a line, engrave a mark, and then to write, and produced scriba, scriptor and scriptura.
items.cn: scribo、scribere 意为「划线、刻记」，进而指书写，并生出 scriba（书记）、scriptor（作者）与 scriptura（文字）。

items.en: The preposition trans meant across or beyond, as in transferre, to carry across.
items.cn: 介词 trans 意为「横过、越过」，如 transferre「搬运过去」。

items.en: Transcribere and transscribere, with an s that some medieval writers dropped, meant to copy out something written elsewhere.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 transcribere、transscribere（有的抄手省去中间的 s）意为「把别处的文字抄写出来」。

items.en: The English verb, spelled transcribe, is recorded in the sixteenth century in the senses of copying a text and of using musical notes for a different voice.
items.cn: 英语动词 transcribe 于十六世纪有记录，既有「抄写文本」义，也有「为另一个人声改记音符」义。

items.en: Phonetic and genetic uses arrived in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, keeping the same copy-across image.
items.cn: 标音与基因两个用法分别出现在十九、二十世纪，仍保留「跨抄过去」的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the same writing root, and the near-meaning group holds words for turning speech into text.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「书写」词根构成的词族；近义组收把话语变成文字的一类词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or the written result of transcribing.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加后缀构成的名词，义为「转写；文字稿；标音；转录」。

entries.definition: A written copy or record, such as the text of a speech or a school record.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，义为「文字稿、抄本、成绩单」。

entries.definition: A person or a device that transcribes.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加后缀构成，义为「转写员、转录设备」。

entries.definition: To say what something is like; de- instead of trans- changes the direction of the writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「描述」，把 trans- 换成 de-，书写方向随之改变。

entries.definition: To arrange to receive something, or to sign beneath a text; sub- means under.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「订阅、在下签名」，前缀 sub- 表示「在下」。

entries.definition: The finished written text, rather than the act of writing it.
entries.definitionCN: 已经写完的文字稿，与 transcribe 表示的「动作」相对。

entries.definition: To write down or capture so that later people can look back.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「记录」，强调把内容留存下来供日后查看。

entries.definition: To reproduce something; neutral about whether it is carried across a sense.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「复制」，不强调是否从一种形式跨到另一种形式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real parts trans- and scribere, the word family and the phrases the verb appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的构件 trans- 与 scribere，以及这个词的词族与常见搭配。

normal.en: trans- means across and scribere means to write, so transcribe is to write across.
normal.cn: trans- 意为「横越」，scribere 意为「写」，所以 transcribe 就是「横着写过去」。

normal.en: The noun transcription and the person transcriber are built on the same verb.
normal.cn: 名词 transcription 与表示人的 transcriber 都由这个动词构成。

normal.en: A transcript is what you get after someone transcribes; the noun adds no new root.
normal.cn: transcript 是别人转写之后得到的东西，这个名词没有引入新词根。

normal.en: Phonetic transcription is how sounds get letters: sound carried across into symbols.
normal.cn: phonetic transcription 是给声音配字母：把声音跨写成符号。

normal.en: Compare describe and subscribe: de- is down from, sub- is under, trans- is across.
normal.cn: 对比 describe 与 subscribe：de- 为「向下写」，sub- 为「在下写」，trans- 为「横越写」。

abstract.en: Picture headphones over a page of blank paper, and a pencil writing each sound the moment it ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一副耳机对着空白纸，每个声音一结束，铅笔就把它写下来。

abstract.en: Imagine a candle-lit monk copying a page that is slowly turning into a clean new sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象一位烛光下的修士在抄写，旧书页慢慢变成一张干净的新纸。

abstract.en: Think of one melody leaving a violin and appearing again on a guitar, note by note.
abstract.cn: 想象同一段旋律离开小提琴，一个音一个音地出现在吉他上。

examples.en: Please transcribe the voicemail and send me the text.
examples.cn: 请把语音留言转写成文字发给我。

examples.en: The librarian transcribed the old ledger for the digital archive.
examples.cn: 图书管理员为数字档案抄录了那本旧账簿。

examples.en: Enzymes transcribe only certain regions of the chromosome.
examples.cn: 酶只转录染色体上的某些区段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿斯克瑞布」——把声音「穿」进纸上的字里，就是听写转写；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（横越、越过）+ scribere（书写）→ 中世纪拉丁语 transcribere（抄写过来）→ 英语 transcribe；核心义「把内容跨抄成另一种形式」，故有抄写、听写转写、乐谱译写、标音与基因转录。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all carry one idea: information moves across from a voice, a page, an instrument or a gene and is written again in a new medium.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都贯穿同一个想法：信息从声音、书页、乐器或基因这一端跨到另一端，在新的介质上重新写出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice or an old page is carried across, letter by letter, onto a fresh sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段声音或一页旧文，被一个字母一个字母地搬到新纸上。

branches.en: THE VOICE: speech is caught and written, either by a careful listener or by a professional transcriber.
branches.cn: 声音线：说出的话被听下写成文字，或由专业转写员完成。

branches.en: THE PAGE: the oldest sense, copying a text from one sheet to another.
branches.cn: 纸面线：最古老的义项，把文本从一张纸抄到另一张纸。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: the same notes are written again for another voice or instrument.
branches.cn: 乐器线：同一组音符为别的乐器或人声重新书写。

branches.en: THE SYMBOL: unwritten sound is carried across into phonetic symbols.
branches.cn: 符号线：没有文字的声音被跨写成音标符号。

branches.en: THE GENE: biology reuses the copying image for DNA read into RNA, alongside the old image of copying a text.
branches.cn: 基因线：生物学把抄写的画面借给 DNA 读出成 RNA，与古老的抄文画面并列。

intro.en: Transcribe is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin writing verb, and the English family grows by ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: transcribe 由拉丁语前缀与拉丁语表示「书写」的动词构成，英语词族再靠普通后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin trans means across, and scribere means to write; both are recorded in classical Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trans 意为「横越」，scribere 意为「书写」，二者都是古典拉丁语中实际存在的词。

items.example: The prefix marks a movement from one side to the other.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出从一侧到另一侧的移动。

items.example: The verb is the writing root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族中表示「书写」的词根。

items.example: Many English verbs end in -scribe.
items.exampleCN: 许多英语动词以 -scribe 结尾。

items.example: The form appears in transcript and script.
items.exampleCN: 这一形式出现在 transcript 与 script 中。

items.example: It forms transcription.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transcription。

items.meaning: one who or that which does
items.example: It forms transcriber.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transcriber。

items.example: It forms transcriptase.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transcriptase。

items.example: It forms transcribable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transcribable。

items.example: The -ive ending builds the adjective transcriptive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成形容词 transcriptive。

latinEntries.example: Scribe and scriptor grow from the same verb.
latinEntries.exampleCN: scribe 与 scriptor 由同一动词生来。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「转写；文字稿；标音；转录」
由动词加表示「做……的人」的后缀构成，义为「转写员」
由 transcript 加表示「酶」的后缀构成，义为「转录酶」

definition_zh: 转写；抄写；文字稿；标音（音标转写）；转录（基因信息转录成 RNA）
definition_en: the act of writing something down from speech or another source, the written text so produced, the use of phonetic symbols, or the copying of a gene into RNA
core_image: 录音机旁边放着一段逐字打出的文字稿，每个声音都有对应的字
scene: 法庭书记员把证人说的话一字不差地打进电脑。The court relies on a full transcription of the witness evidence.
sceneCN: 这里 transcription 是「转写出的文字稿」（第 1 个义项：把口语转写成文字的过程或成品）；句意：法庭依据的是证人证言逐字转写的全文。

pos.zh: 名词：转写；抄写；文字稿；标音；转录

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀得到的动词，义为「转写；抄写；标音；转录」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「转录的；与转录有关的」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「与转写有关的」

senses.title: The act of writing down speech
senses.titleCN: 把口述或录音转写成文字
senses.definition: the process of putting spoken words or a recording into written form
senses.definitionCN: 把说出的话或录音写成文字的过程
senses.example: The interview transcription took four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 把访谈转写成文字花了四个小时。
senses.why: The noun turns the Latin image of writing across into an act: speech crossing over from voice to page.
senses.whyCN: 名词把拉丁语「跨写」的画面变成一个动作：话语从声音跨到纸面。

senses.title: The written text itself
senses.definition: a written copy of what was said or broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 把说过或播出的内容写成的文字副本
senses.example: A transcription of the hearing was sent to both parties.
senses.exampleCN: 听证会的文字稿已送达双方。
senses.why: Once the writing across is finished, the result can be held, filed and quoted, so the noun also names the finished sheet.
senses.whyCN: 跨写一旦完成，结果就能被拿在手上、归档和引用，因此名词也指那张写完的纸。

senses.title: Learned copying of manuscripts
senses.definition: a hand-made copy of a written work, especially an ancient or copied manuscript
senses.definitionCN: 手工抄录的作品文本，尤指古籍或抄本
senses.example: The monastery kept a careful transcription of the charter.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院保存了该特许状的一份仔细抄本。
senses.why: This is the noun at its oldest: the work of a scribe carrying a text across from one manuscript to another.
senses.whyCN: 这是名词最古老的形态：抄手把文本从一部手稿横向搬到另一部手稿上的成品。

senses.title: A system of phonetic symbols
senses.definition: a way of writing sounds with special symbols, often for dictionary entries
senses.definitionCN: 用专门符号记录语音的方法，常见于词典条目
senses.example: The phonetic transcription shows where the stress falls.
senses.exampleCN: 音标转写标出了重音落在哪里。
senses.why: Sound is itself transcribable: the same act of writing across turns breath and voicing into visible symbols.
senses.whyCN: 声音本身可以被转写：同一个「跨写」动作把气流与声带振动变成看得见的符号。

senses.title: Genetic transcription
senses.definition: the process by which a strand of RNA is made from a sequence of DNA
senses.definitionCN: 以 DNA 序列为模板合成一条 RNA 的过程
senses.example: Transcription turns DNA into messenger RNA in the nucleus.
senses.exampleCN: 转录在细胞核内把 DNA 变成信使 RNA。
senses.why: Biology took the naming because genetic information is copied across from one molecule to another, just as text is copied across to a new sheet.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用这个词的命名，是因为遗传信息从一个分子跨抄到另一个分子，正如文本被抄到新纸上。

senses.title: Musical arrangement for another medium
senses.definition: a version of a musical piece rewritten for a different instrument or voice
senses.definitionCN: 为其他乐器或人声改写而成的乐曲版本
senses.example: His transcription of the Bach fugue for brass is well known.
senses.exampleCN: 他把巴赫赋格改写为铜管乐器的版本颇为知名。
senses.why: When notes leave one instrument and are written again for another, the noun names the copy that has been carried across.
senses.whyCN: 音符离开一种乐器、为另一种乐器重新书写时，名词指的就是那份被跨搬过去的新稿。

intro.en: Transcription is the Latin noun for writing across, from transcribere, which joins trans-, across, with scribere, to write.
intro.cn: transcription 是拉丁语中表示「跨写」的名词，来自 transcribere，由 trans-（横越）与 scribere（书写）组合而成。

items.en: The root of scribere and Greek graphein is generally reconstructed as *sker-, to cut or scratch; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为 scribere 与希腊语 graphein 的词根为 *sker-，意为「刻、划」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Scribo, scribere, scriptum meant to engrave a mark and then to write, and gave scriptor and scriptura.
items.cn: scribo、scribere、scriptum 由「刻记号」引申为「书写」，并生出 scriptor 与 scriptura。

items.en: Trans meant across or beyond, and the compound transcribed the idea of something written over from elsewhere.
items.cn: trans 意为「横过、越过」，复合词表达「把别处的东西写过来」。

items.en: Transcription, the noun of action, was used for copying out a text, from transcribere or the later transscribere.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用表示动作的名词 transcription 指抄出文本，源自动词 transcribere 或后来变形的 transscribere。

items.en: English borrowed the noun through French and learned Latin, first for copying manuscripts, later for writing down speech and music.
items.cn: 英语经法语与学术拉丁语借入名词，先指抄录手稿，后指记录口语与音乐。

items.en: The phonetic sense came in the nineteenth century and the genetic sense in the twentieth, keeping the copy-across core.
items.cn: 标音义十九世纪出现，基因义二十世纪出现，都保留了「跨抄」的核心。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same writing root, and the near-meaning group gathers outputs of speech put into text.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「书写」词根的各个形式；近义组收把话语变成文字的成品与相关说法。

entries.definition: The verb that names the act whose result is a transcription.
entries.definitionCN: 与本词对应的动词，指动词本身，本词指它的动作或成品。

entries.definition: A written record, with the stress on the finished copy.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，义为「文字稿、记录」，更强调完成的副本。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to transcription.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「转录的、与转录有关的」。

entries.definition: A doctor written order for medicine; pre- means before, so the writing comes first.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「处方」，前缀 pre- 表示「先前」，写作在前。

entries.definition: An account of what something is like; de- means down, so the writing is set down.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「描述」，前缀 de- 表示「向下」，文字被写下来。

entries.definition: The text itself, common in legal and educational records.
entries.definitionCN: 近义名词，指文本本身，常见于法律与教育记录。

entries.definition: A permanent account of events, wider than a word-for-word transcription.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「记录」，指对事件的永久记载，比逐字转写范围更宽。

entries.definition: A short written remark, not the full words spoken.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「笔记、备注」，只写简短要点，不是全部原话。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real parts trans- and script, the verb transcribe and common phrases such as phonetic transcription.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的构件 trans- 与 script、动词 transcribe，以及 phonetic transcription 之类常见搭配。

normal.en: Transcription is trans- across plus script writing plus -ion; writing across, as a thing.
normal.cn: transcription 就是 trans-「横越」加 script「写」再加 -ion，把「跨写」变成一个名词。

normal.en: The verb transcribe gives the noun -tion, just as describe gives description.
normal.cn: 动词 transcribe 加 -tion 得到名词，正如 describe 加 -tion 得到 description。

normal.en: A phonetic transcription is the written form of sounds, so it belongs to the same root as script.
normal.cn: phonetic transcription 是声音的书写形式，属于同一个 script 词根。

normal.en: In biology transcription is DNA copied into RNA, and translation is RNA turned into protein.
normal.cn: 生物学的 transcription 是 DNA 抄成 RNA，而 translation 是把 RNA 变成蛋白质。

normal.en: Compare transcript: transcript is the paper, transcription is the act or the result of copying.
normal.cn: 对比 transcript：transcript 是那张纸，transcription 侧重抄写的动作或结果。

abstract.en: Picture a recorder and a page side by side, with every sound marked by a matching letter.
abstract.cn: 想象录音机与纸页并排，每个声音都被一个对应的字母标出。

abstract.en: Imagine a voice made of bubbles drifting across a page and drying there as ink.
abstract.cn: 想象由气泡组成的声音飘过纸面，落下来晾干成墨迹。

abstract.en: Think of a single melody stepping from one instrument to the next, written fresh each time.
abstract.cn: 想象一段旋律从一件乐器走向另一件乐器，每次都被重新写下。

examples.en: Please check the transcription against the audio before publishing.
examples.cn: 发表前请对照音频核对转写稿。

examples.en: Her transcription of the song for flute delighted the audience.
examples.cn: 她把那首歌改编成长笛曲，令观众十分欣喜。

examples.en: Transcription of the gene begins at the promoter region.
examples.cn: 该基因的转录从启动子区域开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿斯克里普申」——把声音「穿」写成纸上的字，这份文字就是转写稿；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（横越）+ scribere（书写，过去分词词干 script-）→ 中世纪拉丁语 transcription（抄出文本的动作与结果）→ 英语 transcription；核心义「跨抄而成的文字」，故有听写转写、文字稿、抄本、音标转写与基因转录。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of transcription all name the same crossing of information: something spoken, written, sounded, played or encoded moves across and is written again in a new form.
sensesIntro.cn: transcription 的六个义项都指同一种信息的跨越：说出的话、写下的文、发出的音、演奏的乐或编码的基因，跨过去之后以新的形式被重新写出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a recorder beside a sheet of text, each sound with its own letters.
core.cn: 核心意象：录音机旁放着一张文字稿，每个声音都有对应的文字。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE RESULT: speech put into writing is first a process and then a document.
branches.cn: 动作与成品线：把话语写成文字，先是过程，后是文档。

branches.en: THE MANUSCRIPT: a scribe carries a text across from an older copy.
branches.cn: 手稿线：抄手把文本从更早的抄本搬抄过来。

branches.en: THE SYMBOL: sound itself is written with a special alphabet.
branches.cn: 符号线：声音本身用专门字母记录下来。

branches.en: THE GENE: information is copied across from DNA into RNA.
branches.cn: 基因线：信息从 DNA 跨抄进 RNA。

branches.en: THE MUSIC: notes, like words, are carried across for another voice, sharing the act-result core.
branches.cn: 音乐线：音符像词语一样被跨搬到另一件乐器上，与动作—成品线共享核心。

intro.en: Transcription is a Latin prefix plus a Latin writing verb plus a noun suffix, and the English family grows around transcribe.
intro.cn: transcription 由拉丁语前缀、拉丁语表示「书写」的动词与名词后缀构成，英语词族围绕动词 transcribe 展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin trans means across, scribere means to write, and the noun transcription is recorded in medieval Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trans 意为「横越」，scribere 意为「书写」，名词 transcription 在中世纪拉丁语中有记录。

items.example: The prefix marks the crossing from one form to another.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出从一种形式跨到另一种形式。

items.example: The form sits between trans- and -ion in this word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词中 -script 夹在 trans- 与 -ion 之间。

items.example: The suffix makes it a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀使它成为表示动作的名词。

items.example: The -s changes to t before the suffix.
items.exampleCN: 加后缀前，词干中的 s 变为 t。

items.example: The verb is the writing core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整词的书写核心。

items.example: It forms transcriptional.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transcriptional。

items.example: It forms transcriptive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transcriptive。

items.example: It forms transcriptase, the enzyme of transcription.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transcriptase，即参与转录的酶。

items.example: It forms transcribable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transcribable。

derivatives.zh: 去名词后缀后的动词，义为「转写；抄写；标音；转录」
加形容词后缀构成，义为「转录的」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「与转写有关的」

definition_zh: 转基因；转入基因；转移进新的生物体的外源基因；基因工程中转入的实验基因
definition_en: a gene taken from one organism and introduced into the cells of another, so that the receiving organism carries and often uses that foreign gene
core_image: 一小段基因被从一株植物的细胞里取出，装进另一株的细胞里
scene: 实验室里，科学家把一段外来的基因注入小鼠的受精卵，看它能否遗传给后代。The researchers inserted the transgene into a rice plant to help it resist drought.
sceneCN: 这里 transgene 是「转基因」（第 1 个义项：被人工转入另一生物体、并在那里表达的基因）；句意：研究者把这段转基因插入水稻，使其更耐旱。

pos.zh: 名词：转基因；转入基因；外源基因

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「转基因的、含转入了外源基因的」
由形容词加 -s 构成，义为「转基因学、转基因技术」
由词根加 -genesis「产生」构成，义为「转基因作用、转基因操作」

senses.title: The foreign gene itself
senses.definition: the gene that has been moved from one organism and put into another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种生物中取出并放进另一种生物体内的基因
senses.example: The transgene came from a bacterium that resists insects.
senses.exampleCN: 这段转基因来自一种抗虫细菌。
senses.why: The word is trans, across, plus gene, so its first sense is simply the piece of DNA that has been carried across an organism.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 trans「横越」与 gene「基因」构成，所以第一义就是那段被跨过物种搬过去的 DNA。

senses.title: Artificial insertion for research or farming
senses.titleCN: 人工转入的实验或农业用基因
senses.definition: such a gene inserted on purpose by genetic engineering, for an experiment, a crop or a useful product
senses.definitionCN: 为实验、作物或有用产物而通过基因工程有意插入的这类基因
senses.example: The lab plants a transgene that makes the mouse glow green.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室植入一段使小鼠发绿光的转基因。
senses.why: Because the gene crossed over by human hands rather than by mating, the word carries a strongly artificial, modern-science flavour.
senses.whyCN: 因为这段基因是由人的手而不是繁殖跨过去的，所以这个词带着强烈的人为、现代科学的色彩。

senses.title: A gene inherited across generations
senses.titleCN: 可遗传给后代的转入基因
senses.definition: an inserted gene that becomes part of the germ line and passes to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 被插入并进入生殖细胞系、能传给后代的外源基因
senses.example: Half the seedlings inherited the transgene from the parent plant.
senses.exampleCN: 一半的幼苗从亲本植株遗传到了转基因。
senses.why: Once the gene settles into the chromosomes, it behaves like any inherited gene, so the across image is now a crossing into later generations.
senses.whyCN: 这段基因一旦落进染色体，就会像任何遗传基因一样起作用，于是「横越」的画面变成了跨向后代。

senses.title: A marker or tool in research
senses.titleCN: 研究中的标记或工具基因
senses.definition: a gene used as a marker or test tool in the lab
senses.definitionCN: 实验室里当作标记或检测工具使用的外源基因
senses.example: The transgene acts as a marker that reveals where the cells travel.
senses.exampleCN: 这段转基因充当标记，显示细胞移动到了哪里。
senses.why: In the lab the inserted gene is often not the desired product at all but a visible tool, so the word also names genes used for detection.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，插入的基因常常不是要的产物，而是一件看得见的工具，所以这个词也指用于检测的基因。

intro.en: Transgene is a modern coinage, made from the established elements trans- and gene rather than inherited from Latin as a whole word.
intro.cn: transgene 是现代新造词，由已有的构件 trans- 与 gene 拼成，而不是从拉丁语整体继承来的词。

items.en: Greek genos meant family or birth, and gignesthai meant to be born; this is the source of the gene family.
items.cn: 希腊语 genos 意为「族、出生」，gignesthai 意为「出生」，这是 gene 一族的来源。

items.en: Latin trans, across or beyond, is the prefix of transfer, transplant and transform.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trans 意为「横过、越过」，是 transfer、transplant、transform 的前缀。

items.en: The Danish geneticist Wilhelm Johannsen proposed the word gene in 1909, and English took it quickly.
items.cn: 丹麦遗传学家约翰森在 1909 年提出 gene 一词，英语很快接受。

items.en: Dutch geneticists coined the adjective transgenic for mice given genes from another species; the noun transgene followed as genetics became a field.
items.cn: 荷兰遗传学家为获得了别种生物基因的小鼠造出形容词 transgenic；随着遗传学成为一门学科，名词 transgene 随之出现。

items.en: Today the word covers plants, animals, fish and cells, always meaning a gene moved across, usually by engineering.
items.cn: 如今这个词覆盖植物、动物、鱼类与细胞，恒定含义是「被跨过来搬过去的基因」，通常靠工程手段完成。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same gene root, and the near-meaning group holds related genetics terms about foreign or inherited genes.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一 gene 词根构成的词；近义组收涉及外源基因与遗传的遗传学相关词。

entries.definition: An adjective describing an organism that carries a foreign gene.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ic 构成的形容词，义为「转基因的」，形容带有外源基因的生物。

entries.definition: The field or technique of moving genes between organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 由形容词加 -s 构成的名词，义为「转基因技术、转基因学」。

entries.definition: A unit of DNA that carries information, the second half of this compound.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「基因」，是 DNA 上携带信息的单位，也是本复合词的后半部分。

entries.definition: The full set of genes in an organism.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「基因组」，指一种生物全部基因的集合。

entries.definition: To move a plant or organ to another place; it shares the across prefix, not the gene root.
entries.definitionCN: 同前缀词，义为「移植」，与 transgene 共享「横越」前缀，但词根不是 gene。

entries.definition: One of the forms of an existing gene, with no crossing between organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「等位基因」，是已有基因的某一版本，不涉及物种之间的跨搬。

entries.definition: A change in a gene sequence; it can arise naturally and involves no transfer.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「突变」，指基因序列的改变，可以自然发生，不涉及转移。

entries.definition: A small ring of bacterial DNA often used to carry a gene into cells.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「质粒」，常被用作把基因运进细胞的载体。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real parts trans- and gene plus the well-known adjective transgenic and laboratory phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的构件 trans- 与 gene，以及广为人知的形容词 transgenic 与实验室搭配。

normal.en: Transgene is trans- across and gene: a gene carried across into another organism.
normal.cn: transgene 就是 trans-「横越」加 gene：被横跨着搬进另一个生物体的基因。

normal.en: Its adjective is transgenic, so a transgenic mouse is a mouse that carries a transgene.
normal.cn: 它的形容词是 transgenic，所以 transgenic mouse 就是携带转基因的小鼠。

normal.en: The word is a modern compound; it is not an old Latin word and has no ancient ancestors of its own.
normal.cn: 这个词是现代复合词，不是古拉丁语的整词，本身没有古老的祖先词。

normal.en: Transplant moves an organ across bodies; transgene moves a gene across organisms.
normal.cn: transplant 是把器官跨接在身体之间，transgene 是把基因跨接在物种之间。

normal.en: Compare plasmid: the plasmid is the vehicle, and the transgene is the cargo it carries.
normal.cn: 对比 plasmid：质粒是运送工具，transgene 是它运送的货物。

abstract.en: Picture a note written in one creature being slipped into the pocket of another.
abstract.cn: 想象写着一种生物密码的纸条，被悄悄塞进另一种生物的口袋。

abstract.en: Imagine a door in a cell wall opening for one small gene to walk through and stay.
abstract.cn: 想象细胞壁上的门为一小段基因打开，让它走进并留下来。

abstract.en: Think of a seed that now carries a foreign instruction, and that instruction is copied into its children.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子带上了一条外来的指令，这条指令又被抄进它的后代。

examples.en: Scientists inserted a transgene into the maize to resist a common pest.
examples.cn: 科学家向玉米中插入一段抗常见害虫的转基因。

examples.en: Tests confirmed that the transgene was present in three of the fish.
examples.cn: 检测确认其中三条鱼体内含有该转基因。

examples.en: The transgene is passed from parent to offspring in about half the cases.
examples.cn: 大约一半的情况下，该转基因会从亲本传给后代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿斯基因」——一段基因「穿」过物种的边界，搬进另一个身体里；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（横越、越过）+ 现代英语 gene（基因，源自希腊语 genos「族、出生」）；该词为二十世纪后期现代复合词，义为「被跨物种搬入的基因」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of transgene all describe one piece of DNA that has crossed into a new host, whether as foreign material, as an engineering choice, as an inherited trait, or as a lab marker.
sensesIntro.cn: transgene 的四个义项都围绕同一段 DNA：它跨进了新的宿主，或被当作外来物质，或出于工程选择，或成为可遗传的特征，或作为实验室标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small strip of DNA taken from one cell and tucked into another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小段 DNA 从一个细胞里取出，再塞进另一个细胞。

branches.en: THE DNA ITSELF: the foreign gene as a piece of material.
branches.cn: DNA 本身线：带着外来身份的那段基因物质。

branches.en: THE ENGINEER: the gene goes across by human design, for a crop, a lab or a product.
branches.cn: 工程线：基因因人的设计跨过去，用于作物、实验或产品。

branches.en: THE GENERATION: the inserted gene settles in the chromosomes and passes to offspring.
branches.cn: 世代线：插入的基因落进染色体，传给后代，与第一义互为表里。

branches.en: THE TOOL: a visible gene used to reveal where cells go.
branches.cn: 工具线：用一段看得见的基因显示细胞的去向。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: every sense crosses an organism boundary, whether by chance, by design or through inheritance.
branches.cn: 边界线：所有义项都跨越了物种边界，或出自设计，或经由遗传。

intro.en: Transgene is a modern compound of a Latin prefix and a modern noun, and English grows transgenic, transgenics and transgenesis from it.
intro.cn: transgene 是拉丁语前缀与现代名词组成的现代复合词，英语由它生出 transgenic、transgenics 与 transgenesis。

latinIntro.en: Only the prefix trans is classical; gene comes through German genetics from the Greek root genos, family or birth.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前缀 trans 是古典词；gene 经由德国遗传学从希腊语词根 genos「族、出生」而来。

items.example: The prefix shows the gene crossing a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示基因越过了边界。

items.example: The second part names the unit of heredity.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分指遗传单位。

items.example: The root appears in genetics and genome.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在 genetics 与 genome 中。

items.example: It forms transgenic.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transgenic。

items.example: It forms transgenics.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transgenics。

items.example: It forms transgenesis.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transgenesis。

items.example: It forms genome from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根加 -ome 构成 genome。

items.example: It forms genotype, the genetic make-up of a cell.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 genotype，指细胞的遗传组成。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「转基因的」
由形容词加 -s 构成，义为「转基因技术」
由词根加 -genesis 构成，义为「转基因作用」
